epics.title: E01 — Playable Vertical Slice
epics.description:
## Outcome
A player can start the game from a title screen, pick a class, spawn into a grey-box room, walk a corridor, fight a skeleton, loot it, save, die, respawn and reload — end to end, in a browser, verified by an automated e2e test. At m2 a grey-box class gauntlet proves every class's core verbs in one course.

## Scope
- In: title → class select → spawn flow; the pause menu (resume / settings / save / load / quit to title); the m1 grey-box slice level; the player death & respawn loop (consumes the combat Died event and e30-death-reload); contextual respawn rules used later by the Knot (wake in the Fold); area transitions between scenes; the m1 "slice plays start-to-finish" e2e + perf test; the m2 class-fantasies gauntlet level and its per-class e2e runs.
- Out: the systems themselves (controller E02, combat E04, saves E30, inventory E17, loot E18); final art/audio (E37/E38); the real MVP levels (E24–E26).

## Exit criteria
- The m1 slice e2e passes in CI on Chromium on every PR.
- Death → respawn/reload returns to play in <= 3 s warm.
- The m2 gauntlet is completed by a scripted replay for each of the four classes using only that class's verbs.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 [e2e] Given a clean browser profile, when the slice e2e runs, then it reaches "slice complete" with zero console errors.
- EC-2 [e2e] Given each of the four classes, when its gauntlet replay runs, then the course is completed using only that class's capabilities.

epics.title: E13 — Bestiary
epics.description:
## Outcome
The ten MVP creature types from the story bible (the Forgotten, Rootcellar Goblins, Brother Horn, Loom Spiders, Briar Wolves, Hushlings, Tallow Ooze, Mimics, Hollow Sentinels, the Sleepless Abbot) exist as data on e12-creature-schema with behaviours, property-driven vulnerabilities, readable telegraphed attacks and at least one avoid/trick option each. Horn and the Abbot have authored boss encounters.

## Scope
- In: creature data, move sets, vulnerabilities via world properties, factions, song-intensity modulation, boss encounter logic, readability/avoidability CI audit, tuning.
- Out: creature framework/AI runtime (E11/E12); dialogue and non-combat relationships (E14/E39); level placement (E24–E26); creature models and audio (E37/E38).

## Exit criteria
- Every MVP creature validates, spawns in the creature arena and has an automated test per declared vulnerability and avoid option.
- Every creature attack passes the readability rule (windup >= 300 ms; unblockable/grab >= 500 ms with distinct cue).
- The Forgotten skeleton ships in m1.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 [integration] Given the bestiary audit, when CI runs, then all ten creature types pass readability and avoidability checks.
- EC-2 [manual] Given an internal playtest, when players meet each creature, then each creature is described by >= 3 of 5 testers by a behaviour, not only by its damage.

epics.title: E14 — Social Creatures
epics.description:
## Outcome
The Rootcellar goblins (Mother Kettleback, Snig), Clatter the skeleton who remembers, Brother Horn and Mortimer the book mimic can be talked to, fed, gifted, calmed, befriended and helped — not only fought — using e22 dialogue/disposition/gifts and e12 dispositions/affordances, with outcomes persisted as world facts.

## Scope
- In: humming the Vesper hymn as a player verb; creature-side social behaviour, affordances, disposition rules, gift preferences, befriend/help state machines, follower/ally behaviour where required; scenario tests for every social path.
- Out: dialogue text (e39-dialogue-*); quest graphs (e39-main-quest-data, e39-side-quests-*); dialogue/disposition runtimes (E22/E12); combat move sets (E13).

## Exit criteria
- Every social path in bible §4.2, §5.9–5.11 and §6.1 is reachable in an automated scenario and sets the documented facts.
- No social creature path dead-ends: failure always lands in a new state.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 [integration] Given the social scenario suite, when run in CI, then every declared path reaches its outcome fact.
- EC-2 [manual] Given a playtest, when testers meet Horn, then >= 2 of 5 discover a non-combat resolution unprompted.

epics.title: E16 — Class-Specific Solutions
epics.description:
## Outcome
Every mandatory obstacle in the MVP has deliberate routes for knight, archer, sorcerer and thief (at least three of four, target four), documented in a route matrix, declared as data, proved by replays and enforced by a CI audit.

## Scope
- In: route-matrix document; obstacle registry data; CI audit reusing e15-solution-audit class capability profiles and e19-capability-registry ids; route replays; gap-closing authoring passes; per-class playtest.
- Out: the capabilities themselves (E04/E05/E08/E10); puzzle-level audits (e15-solution-audit); per-area first-pass routes (the class-route items in E24/E25/E26).

## Exit criteria
- CI fails if any mandatory obstacle has fewer than 3 validated class routes.
- Each class completes the MVP critical path in a playtest using its own fantasy.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 [integration] Given the obstacle registry, when the route audit runs, then every mandatory obstacle reports >= 3 validated class routes.
- EC-2 [manual] Given one playtester per class, when they finish the MVP, then each reports >= 3 moments where their class opened a route others could not.

epics.title: E24 — Briar Glen
epics.description:
## Outcome
Briar Glen is a dense, lived-in settlement: every named building from the story bible exists and is enterable, merchants and the Lamplit Stacks have authored stock, named NPCs keep day/night schedules, rumours point at real places, rooftops and secrets reward thieves and the curious, and the first-night sleepwalk plays out through its streets.

## Scope
- In: world map/connectivity doc; day/night content on the e27-world-clock; town blockout; the Sleeping Ox, Lamplit Stacks, Forge, Fletchery & Simples, Bakery, Watch House and jail, Vane House, schoolhouse, Glen Well → cistern, cemetery; rooftop/thief routes; NPC placement and schedules; merchant stock; rumour and secret placement; first-night staging; class routes; art-dress, lighting/audio and perf passes.
- Out: dialogue text (E39); quest graphs (E39); shop/bookshop/dialogue runtimes (E20/E21/E22); the priory end of the cistern (E26); final assets (E37/E38).

## Exit criteria
- All bible §3.5 town locations exist, are reachable and have at least one interaction.
- Town hits the hardware-baseline perf budgets with the full NPC population.
- Every town rumour resolves to a fact produced by placed content.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 [e2e] Given a new game, when the town tour replay visits every named building, then each interior loads and its key interactable responds.
- EC-2 [perf] Given Market Green at midday with the full schedule population, when measured, then High preset p95 frame time <= 16.7 ms on the reference machine.

epics.title: E25 — Wilderness Region
epics.description:
## Outcome
The Briarwood, Mooring's Watch, the River Wend and the Deepworks' exterior approach form an interconnected wilderness around Briar Glen: the Sleepers' Path, the Standing Horn, the wolf den, the woodcutter's hut, the millpond and drowned lane, the watchtower with its signal mirror and supply tunnel, and the boarded mine gate, plus the river (Briar Glen Quay and the Ore Stair, the Millweir sluice walk, the Weeping Adit into the lower mine, the towpath and Kestrel Lock, and barge travel to Wendmouth) — with loops and shortcuts unlocked by abilities.

## Scope
- In: Briarwood, Mooring's Watch and River Wend blockout; barge travel service (narrated ride / fast travel — no flowing-water sim; e03 rules apply to standing water); encounters, set pieces, the mine-gate "getting in" obstacle, shortcuts, secrets, class routes, art/lighting/audio/perf passes.
- Decision: the Deepworks INTERIOR lives in E26 (First Dungeon), because the bible and constitution treat mine → priory → Knot as one dungeon network with shared encounter, puzzle and shortcut logic. E25 owns everything outside the mine gate, the watchtower supply tunnel up to the collapse, the Weeping Adit up to its emergence and the Ore Stair chute; E26 owns everything inside the mine.
- Out: Deepworks interior, Bellwater Priory and the Knot (E26); town (E24); Wendmouth (E40); creature data (E13).

## Exit criteria
- Every wilderness location in bible §3.5 exists and is reachable from town with the starting kit.
- At least three shortcuts in the region are unlockable and persist.
- Wilderness meets perf budgets with full foliage on both presets.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 [integration] Given the connectivity graph, when validated, then every E25 node is reachable from town with base capabilities of every class.
- EC-2 [perf] Given the densest Briarwood view, when measured, then both preset budgets from the hardware baseline hold.

epics.title: E26 — First Dungeon
epics.description:
## Outcome
One exceptional multi-route dungeon network — the Deepworks mine, Bellwater Priory and the Knot labyrinth (Outer Ring, Ossuary Galleries, Chapel of Echoes, the Fold, Horn's Hall, Sounding Shaft, the Cradle) — combining combat, stealth, the six MVP puzzles, creatures and secrets, ending in the Sounding Shaft climb and the ringing of the Vesper Bell, with level states for all four endings.

## Scope
- In: dungeon layout doc; grey-box blockout per area; encounters and systemic objects; the six MVP puzzles placed from e15 references; rune navigation; shortcuts and loops; Fold respawn point; set pieces (sour bell, Horn's Hall, Cradle, climb, Vespers); ending level variants; class routes; secrets/lore; art/lighting/audio/perf/playtest passes.
- Out: creature behaviour (E13), social logic (E14), quest graphs and text (E39), puzzle framework (E15), final assets (E37/E38).

## Exit criteria
- The dungeon is completable end to end by each class via at least two distinct macro-routes.
- All six MVP puzzles pass the solvability validator in their final placement.
- Each dungeon area meets perf budgets on both presets.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 [e2e] Given a save at the mine gate, when each class's critical-path replay runs, then it reaches "Vespers rung".
- EC-2 [integration] Given the placed puzzles, when e15-solution-audit runs, then all six pass with >= 2 solutions and >= 3 classes.

epics.title: E40 — Wendmouth Harbor
epics.description:
## Outcome
Wendmouth, the rowdy harbour town at the mouth of the River Wend, is an optional-but-rewarding MVP level where shenanigans ensue: sneakiness is richly rewarded (customs house, bonded warehouse, manifests, rooftops, rigging, crowds, the Undertow), every other class gets hijinks (brawls, arm-wrestling, duels, the Gull Shoot, the Regatta, freezing the harbour pool), and everyone can equip themselves better than in Briar Glen (the Tidemarket and the Undertow). The Crate for Mr. S— heist, the Tidefair and Contraband Pages play out here.

## Scope
- In: harbour grey-box; Ore Wharf; Customs House and book confiscation; Bonded Warehouse and bay nine; the Drowned Gull; Tidemarket and Undertow stock data (Tereza Maelo, Nell Gannet, the foreign book cart); rooftop/net-loft route; the Gilded Tern; breakwater, sea-door and tides; crowds and dockhand disguises; human opposition (harbour watch, Low Tide Company, Tern crew); a small contest framework and the Tidefair events; heist placement; class routes; secrets/rumours; art, lighting/audio, perf/playtest.
- Out: new creature types (none — the roster stays at 10); flowing-water or ship simulation (water is standing volumes; barge travel is a narrated ride in e25-barge-travel); quest graphs and dialogue (e39-harbor-*, e39-dialogue-harbor-*); shop/bookshop/crime/disguise runtimes (E20/E21/E22/E10); final assets (E37/E38).
- Constraint: Wendmouth is optional; no main-quest step requires it.

## Exit criteria
- Every bible §3.6 place exists, is reachable by barge and towpath, and hosts at least one interaction.
- The Crate for Mr. S— is solvable by all six routes; every quest-mandatory harbour obstacle passes the E16 audit with >= 3 classes.
- Every class can buy or earn >= 2 items not sold in Briar Glen.
- Market day and the Tidefair brawl meet the hardware-baseline budgets on both presets.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 [integration] Given the six heist route replays, when run in CI, then each sets its crate outcome fact.
- EC-2 [manual] Given 5 testers, when they spend 30 minutes in Wendmouth, then >= 4 report a hijink or heist moment unprompted.

items.title: Write the m1 vertical slice spec and grey-box level plan
items.description:
## Why
M1 is the first proof the game loop works end to end; everyone building toward it needs one shared definition of "done".

## What
docs/design/vertical-slice.md: the exact flow (title → class select → spawn room → corridor → skeleton fight room → loot alcove → locked exit → slice complete), a top-down grey-box sketch with dimensions, which systems each beat exercises, the pass criteria for the e2e test, and what is explicitly faked (placeholder art, one class required, no dialogue).

## Scope
- In: Slice flow, level sketch, beat → system mapping, pass criteria, placeholder list
- Out: Building the level (e01-slice-greybox-level)
- Out: m2 class gauntlet (e01-class-gauntlet-level)

## Notes
Keep the slice under 5 minutes for a first-time player. Related: e35-fun-hypotheses (the slice should be the stimulus for e35-greybox-combat-test).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the spec, when reviewed, then every beat names the owning bead key (e.g. e04-melee-core, e18-containers) of the system it exercises.
- AC-2 [content] Given the spec, when reviewed, then it defines a single machine-checkable "slice complete" condition (world fact slice.complete = true).
- AC-3 [content] Given the spec, when reviewed, then it lists the failure paths in scope (player death, reload with no save, leaving the fight room mid-combat) and their expected outcomes.

items.title: Title screen flows into class select, spawn and continue
items.description:
## Why
The player must be able to "enter the game" (E01 outcome) without developer tools.

## What
As a player, I want a title screen with New Game, Continue and Load so that I can start or resume the slice in two clicks.
New Game → e19 class selection → loads the slice scene at its spawn point with the class kit. Continue loads the most recent save. Load opens e30-save-load-ui. Grey-box styling; build SHA shown (per e35-playtest-builds).

## Scope
- In: Title screen, New Game/Continue/Load wiring, scene hand-off to the slice spawn point
- Out: Class selection screen (e19-class-selection)
- Out: Save/load menus (e30-save-load-ui)
- Out: Final title art/music (E37/E38)

## Notes
The first scene id comes from a data field (game.startScene) so E24 can switch the start to the mountain road at m3 without code.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given a clean profile, when the player clicks New Game, selects Knight and confirms, then the slice spawn room is playable within 10 s of page load on a 50 Mbps connection.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given no saves exist, when the title screen shows, then Continue is disabled and has an accessible "no saves yet" tooltip.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a save exists, when Continue is chosen, then the most recent save loads and the sim state hash equals the saved hash.
- AC-4 [unit] Given game.startScene references a scene id that does not exist, when the content check runs, then it fails naming the missing id.

items.title: Pause the game with resume, settings, save and quit to title
items.description:
## Why
The m1 loop must be playable without dev tools: players need to stop, change settings, save and leave.

## What
As a player, I want Esc (or Start) to pause the game and offer Resume, Settings, Save, Load and Quit to Title so that I control my session.
Pausing halts the sim step (and therefore the world clock). Save is disabled with a reason when the autosave "unsafe" predicate vetoes (combat, mid-air, dialogue). Quit to Title asks for confirmation when there is unsaved progress since the last save. Keyboard and gamepad navigable.

## Scope
- In: Pause overlay on e00-ui-framework, sim pause/resume, wiring to settings, save and load screens, quit-to-title teardown
- Out: Settings screens (e31-settings-framework)
- Out: Save/load screens (e30-save-load-ui)

## Notes
Pause must be deterministic-safe: no sim ticks while paused, so replays are unaffected by pause duration.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the slice running, when Esc is pressed, then the sim stops stepping within one frame and the state hash is unchanged after 10 real seconds paused.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the skeleton is in Combat, when the pause menu opens, then Save is disabled with the reason "Can't save during combat" and Resume still works (edge).
- AC-3 [e2e] Given progress since the last save, when Quit to Title is chosen, then a confirmation appears; on confirm the title screen shows with zero console errors and Continue loads the last save.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the menu opened with a gamepad, when navigating with the d-pad, then every option is reachable with visible focus.

items.title: Build the slice grey-box level: room, corridor, arena, loot, exit
items.description:
## Why
The loop needs a place: a small, readable space that exercises movement, a door, a fight and a reward.

## What
As a player, I want a short grey-box level so that I can explore, fight and loot in one continuous space.
Scene data (content/scenes/slice.json): spawn room with an interactable door, a 20 m corridor with one side alcove, a 12×12 m fight arena with two pillars for spacing, a loot alcove, and an exit door locked by a key. Checkpoint trigger at the arena entrance. Uses only e00 greybox kit pieces.

## Scope
- In: Scene data, navmesh bake, door/lock wiring, checkpoint trigger, slice-complete trigger
- Out: Skeleton spawn (e01-slice-skeleton-encounter)
- Out: Loot (e01-slice-loot)

## Notes
Pillars exist so a knight can break line of attack and so the skeleton's lunge can whiff — combat must be fun without rewards (e04-skeleton-fun-validation).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given slice.json, when validated, then it passes the scene schema and references only greybox kit pieces.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the scene loaded headless, when the navmesh is queried, then a path exists from spawn to exit and the arena is fully connected.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player walks into the exit trigger without the key, when it fires, then the door stays locked and a "locked" prompt appears (no slice complete).
- AC-4 [perf] Given the slice scene, when idling at spawn, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).

items.title: Place the Forgotten skeleton fight in the slice arena
items.description:
## Why
"Fighting a skeleton should be enjoyable even when the player doesn't need XP or loot." The slice's fight is that promise in miniature.

## What
As a player, I want a skeleton that wakes when I enter the arena and fights with readable attacks so that the slice has a real fight.
Spawns e13-forgotten-skeleton (miner variant) seated against the far pillar in a Unaware "resting" idle; enters Combat on sight or on noise in the arena. On death it drops its carried key.

## Scope
- In: Encounter data (spawn, idle, wake trigger), key carried by the skeleton
- Out: Skeleton data and moves (e13-forgotten-skeleton)
- Out: AI (E11)

## Notes
Leaving the arena mid-fight: the skeleton pursues to the corridor then returns to its post (leash 25 m) — failure creates a new situation, not a reset.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the player enters the arena in view of the skeleton, when 2 s elapse, then the skeleton is in Combat state and has targeted the player.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the skeleton is killed, when its Died event fires, then the exit key is dropped as a world item within 1 m of its body.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player flees beyond the 25 m leash, when 10 s pass, then the skeleton returns to its post in Searching then Unaware state and retains its damage (edge).
- AC-4 [manual] Given 3 internal testers, when they play the slice, then each can name at least one skeleton attack by its telegraph.

items.title: Add slice loot: skeleton key drop and an alcove chest
items.description:
## Why
The loop is explore → fight → loot; the reward should matter (it opens the exit) and be interesting (item text with voice).

## What
As a player, I want to loot the skeleton and a chest so that I get the exit key and a small surprise.
The skeleton carries "Rusted gallery key"; the alcove chest uses a slice loot table (a healing draught, a few coins, one oddity with bible-voice text). The exit door accepts the key via the keyring.

## Scope
- In: Item data for the key and oddity, slice loot table, chest placement, door lock id
- Out: Container/loot runtime (E18)
- Out: Keyring (e17-keys-keyring)

## Notes
Item text follows bible §7.4 voice (1–3 sentences with a turn of feeling). Placeholder text is fine until e39-item-creature-text.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the slice loot table, when validated, then it passes e18-loot-validator and every entry references an existing item.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the player holds the gallery key, when interacting with the exit door, then it unlocks and opens without opening the inventory.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the chest has been looted and the game is saved and reloaded, when the chest is opened again, then it is empty (edge).

items.title: Save and reload the slice with world state intact
items.description:
## Why
Save/reload is part of the m1 loop; reloading must restore the world, not just the player.

## What
As a player, I want to save anywhere safe and reload into exactly the same situation so that I trust the game with my time.
Wire the slice to autosave on the arena checkpoint and after slice completion; manual save from the pause menu (e01-pause-menu). Persisted: player vitals/inventory, skeleton alive/dead, chest looted, door state.

## Scope
- In: Checkpoint autosave trigger, fact registrations for slice state, pause-menu save
- Out: Save format, storage and UI (E30)
- Out: World-state store (e27-world-state-store)

## Notes
Autosave must defer while the skeleton is in Combat (e30-autosave safe predicate).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the skeleton is dead and the chest looted, when the game is saved and reloaded, then the skeleton does not respawn, the chest is empty and the sim state hash matches.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the player enters the checkpoint trigger while the skeleton is in Combat, when the trigger fires, then the autosave is deferred until combat ends (edge).
- AC-3 [e2e] Given a manual save in the corridor, when the page is reloaded and Continue chosen, then play resumes in the corridor within 3 s warm.

items.title: Run the player death and respawn loop
items.description:
## Why
E01 owns dying: death must be a quick, clear beat that invites another attempt ("failure creates stories").

## What
As a player, I want dying to play a short death beat and then offer respawn or reload so that I am back in play within seconds.
On the player's Died event (e04-damage-model): freeze input, 1.5 s death beat (camera pull-back, fade), then hand off to the e30-death-reload screen. Adds a data-driven respawn-rule resolver (content/world/respawn-rules.json): rules of {region, conditions, destination, mode: reload|wake-in-place, factsToSet}. m1 ships a single rule: slice → reload last save. Emits player.died and player.respawned telemetry-ready events.

## Scope
- In: Died handling for the player entity, death beat, respawn-rule schema + resolver, m1 rule, events
- Out: Death screen and reload mechanics (e30-death-reload)
- Out: Contextual wake-up rules such as the Fold (e01-contextual-respawn)

## Notes
Coordinate with foundation: e30-death-reload owns the screen and reload; this item owns everything between Died and that screen plus the rule table. Related: e39-failure-narratives (texts), e34-gameplay-events (death telemetry).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the player entity emits Died, when the next tick runs, then player input is ignored and exactly one player.died event is emitted with position and killer id.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given the player dies in the slice arena, when "Load last save" is chosen, then the game is playable within 3 s warm and the skeleton's state matches the save.
- AC-3 [unit] Given two respawn rules whose conditions both match, when resolved, then the rule with the higher priority wins and ties break by rule id deterministically.
- AC-4 [unit] Given no respawn rule matches the current region, when the player dies, then the resolver falls back to reload-last-save and logs a content warning (edge).
- AC-5 [content] Given respawn-rules.json, when validated, then every destination references an existing scene spawn point.

items.title: Prove the slice plays start-to-finish in a CI e2e test
items.description:
## Why
Releases must be trusted without reading the code; the m1 loop is the most important thing to never break.

## What
A Playwright e2e test that boots the build, starts a new game as Knight, drives the slice via a recorded input log (e00-replay-harness) through fight → loot → save → deliberate death → reload → exit, and asserts slice.complete. Also asserts perf and load budgets on the reference CI runner profile.

## Scope
- In: Recorded input log, Playwright spec, CI job wiring, perf/load assertions
- Out: Per-class gauntlet e2e (e01-class-gauntlet-e2e)

## Notes
Replays must be regenerated when controller tuning changes; provide a pnpm script to re-record.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given the CI build, when the slice e2e runs, then it reaches slice.complete = true with zero console errors or unhandled rejections.
- AC-2 [e2e] Given the scripted death step, when the reload completes, then the replay continues and the final sim state hash equals the committed golden hash.
- AC-3 [perf] Given the slice run, when measured, then initial load to playable <= 10 s at 50 Mbps throttling, warm reload <= 3 s and JS heap <= 1.5 GB.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the build is served with IndexedDB unavailable, when the slice runs, then saving shows the documented fallback message and the run still reaches the exit (edge).

items.title: Playtest the m1 slice flow and file follow-up beads
items.description:
## Why
Automated tests prove the loop works; only people prove it is understandable.

## What
Five internal testers play the slice cold with no instructions beyond controls. Observe: time to first attack, whether they find the key, whether death/reload is understood, whether they save voluntarily. Produce docs/playtests/m1-slice.md and beads for every blocker.

## Scope
- In: Session plan, observation notes, findings doc, follow-up beads
- Out: Combat fun validation (e35-greybox-combat-test, e04-skeleton-fun-validation)

## Notes
Run in the same sessions as e35-greybox-combat-test to save tester time.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given 5 testers, when they play, then >= 4 reach slice complete within 8 minutes without help.
- AC-2 [manual] Given testers who die, when the death screen appears, then >= 4 of 5 return to play without asking what to do.
- AC-3 [content] Given the findings doc, when complete, then every issue observed by >= 2 testers has a bead key listed next to it.

items.title: Connect scenes with area transitions and named spawn points
items.description:
## Why
The MVP world is a network (town, forest, tower, mine, priory, labyrinth); players must move between areas seamlessly and saves must survive it.

## What
As a player, I want to walk through a doorway, gate or tunnel into the next area so that the world feels continuous.
Transition volumes reference {targetScene, targetSpawn}; the loader unloads the current scene, persists entity deltas, loads the target, places the player at the spawn with camera facing, and triggers autosave. Loading screen with area name only if load exceeds 500 ms.

## Scope
- In: Transition volume component, spawn point markers, load/unload orchestration, autosave hook, loading overlay
- Out: Asset streaming/compression (e32-asset-loading)
- Out: World connectivity design (e24-world-map-connectivity)

## Notes
Companions/followers (Horn, Snig) transfer with the player if flagged follow=true.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a transition from scene A to B, when the player enters the volume, then B loads, the player stands at the named spawn and A's entity deltas are persisted.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a creature in Combat pursuing the player, when the player transitions, then the creature does not follow unless flagged pursuer, and returns to Searching in A (edge).
- AC-3 [unit] Given a transition referencing a missing spawn id, when content is validated, then validation fails naming the scene and spawn.
- AC-4 [perf] Given a warm cache, when transitioning between two grey-box scenes, then time from trigger to playable <= 3 s on the reference machine.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given 50 back-and-forth transitions, when run in the memory leak harness, then heap growth after GC is <= 5% (ties to e32-memory-leak-test).

items.title: Wake in context after death instead of reloading
items.description:
## Why
Bible §4.5: dying in the Knot wakes you in the Fold, dying in the Briarwood wakes you at the Sleeping Ox. Death must move the story sideways.

## What
As a player, I want to wake somewhere meaningful after I die so that failure becomes part of the story.
Extends the respawn resolver with mode wake-in-place: no reload; the world state is kept; the player is moved to the destination spawn with restored health, set facts (e.g. rescues.byHorn += 1), an optional cost (coin/trinket fee), and a wake text id. Death screen still offers "Load last save" as a secondary option. Rules for Knot → Fold, Knot (Horn dead) → goblin camp or Forgotten laying-out, Briarwood → Sleeping Ox are content in the respective area items.

## Scope
- In: wake-in-place mode, fee/cost effects, counters, wake text hook, death-screen option ordering
- Out: Rule content per area (e26-horns-hall-fold, e25-briarwood-greybox)
- Out: Wake texts (e39-failure-narratives)

## Notes
Creatures that killed the player return to routine; hostile creatures near the wake point are pushed to Searching elsewhere so the player never wakes into a lethal loop.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a wake-in-place rule for region knot with fact horn.alive, when the player dies, then the player is placed at the Fold spawn at full health and rescues.byHorn increments by exactly 1.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a rule with a fee of 20 coins and a player holding 5, when applied, then the fee takes 5 coins and sets fact debt.kettleback = 15 (edge: no negative gold).
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player wakes in place, when inspected, then no world facts or entity deltas are rolled back other than those in factsToSet.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a hostile creature within 15 m of the wake spawn, when the wake completes, then that creature is relocated or set to a non-combat state before input resumes (edge).
- AC-5 [e2e] Given the death screen after a wake-eligible death, when shown, then "Wake" is the default focused option and "Load last save" is available.

items.title: Build the grey-box class gauntlet exercising every class verb
items.description:
## Why
M2 must prove each class fantasy in grey-box: "a locked tower isn't simply requires level 8".

## What
As a player of any class, I want a grey-box course whose every gate has a route for my class so that my class's core verbs are proven.
Five chambers, each with one gate and four routes: (1) Parry gate: skeleton sentry — knight parry/riposte or smash a weak wall; archer headshot from a gallery; sorcerer Gust it off a ledge; thief sneak/backstab. (2) Rope bridge chasm: rope arrow anchor; Levitate/Blink; climb route; knight kicks a beam across. (3) Webbed door: Ember/fire arrow burns web; knight cuts; thief finds vent. (4) Water channel: Frostglass freeze; float crates; climb beams; blunt-arrow the sluice. (5) Guard room with locked chest and lever: lockpick; shoot the lever; Mage Hand it; shield-bash the lock.

## Scope
- In: Scene data for 5 chambers, gate/route wiring, route declarations per class
- Out: The verbs (E04/E05/E08/E10)
- Out: Route audit for the real MVP (E16)

## Notes
Each chamber is also a reusable e16 obstacle template. Every route must work via properties (flammable, climbable, shootable), never pairings.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the gauntlet scene, when validated, then every gate declares >= 3 class routes referencing existing capability ids.
- AC-2 [integration] Given chamber 3's web, when any heat source above its ignition threshold touches it, then it burns away regardless of source (spell, arrow, torch).
- AC-3 [integration] Given a player breaks the chamber 2 beam before crossing, when the chasm is re-evaluated, then at least one remaining route still exists for every class (no softlock, edge).
- AC-4 [perf] Given the densest gauntlet chamber with 4 creatures and fire, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).

items.title: Replay the class gauntlet end to end for each of the four classes
items.description:
## Why
Class fantasies must stay proven as systems change; a regression in any class verb should fail CI.

## What
Four recorded replays (knight, archer, sorcerer, thief) that complete the gauntlet using only class-granted capabilities, asserted headlessly in CI and via Playwright on Chromium nightly.

## Scope
- In: 4 replays, headless CI job, nightly Playwright job, capability-use assertion
- Out: Playtests of class feel (e35-class-fantasy-tests)

## Notes
The capability-use assertion reads capability.used events and fails if a replay used a capability outside its class kit.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given each class replay, when run headless, then the gauntlet.complete fact is set and the final hash equals the golden hash.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the thief replay, when capability.used events are inspected, then no event references a capability not granted by the thief class (edge).
- AC-3 [e2e] Given the nightly Chromium run, when all four replays execute, then each finishes with zero console errors.

items.title: Add the Forgotten skeleton with the e04 three-move set
items.description:
## Why
The skeleton is the game's first creature and the m1 fight; it must be fun to fight with no reward.

## What
As a player, I want a skeleton that fights with readable, parryable attacks so that my first fight feels intrinsically good.
Creature data forgotten-miner on e12-creature-schema: walker, sight + hearing, no smell; resistances blunt 1.5, pierce 0.5, poison 0 (per e04 example); adopts the e04-creature-attack-hooks greybox skeleton set exactly: overhead chop (parryable), 2-hit slash (parryable), lunging thrust (unparryable, blockable). Placeholder capsule-plus-bones mesh.

## Scope
- In: Creature data, move references, resistance table, content test
- Out: Crumble/reassemble (e13-forgotten-reassembly)
- Out: Monk variant and habits (e13-forgotten-habits)
- Out: Model/animation (E37)

## Notes
Adopts the e04-creature-attack-hooks greybox skeleton set verbatim. Related: e04-skeleton-fun-validation uses this creature.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given forgotten-miner.json, when validated, then it passes CreatureDef and all three moves pass the readability rule (windup >= 18 ticks; the thrust flagged unparryable).
- AC-2 [integration] Given the knight parries the overhead chop in window, when resolved, then the skeleton enters Parried and a riposte is available.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a 30-blunt hit, when resolved against the skeleton, then 45 damage is applied; given 30 poison, then 0 and immune feedback (edge).
- AC-4 [integration] Given the creature arena, when spawned, then it ticks 600 frames, perceives a player at 10 m in lit space and enters Combat.

items.title: Write the MVP bestiary design sheet for all ten creatures
items.description:
## Why
Creatures are creatures, not target dummies; each needs behaviours, fears and non-combat options designed before data is authored.

## What
docs/design/bestiary.md: for each of the ten MVP creatures — role, senses, locomotion, faction, move list with telegraph type and timings, vulnerabilities as world properties (never pairings), fears, avoid/trick/social options, placement areas, song-intensity behaviour, and asset needs pointer.

## Scope
- In: Design sheet for all ten creatures
- In: Telegraph table
- In: Property-vulnerability table
- Out: Creature data (per-creature items)
- Out: Creature lore text (e39-item-creature-text)

## Notes
Names and lore must match docs/narrative/story-bible.md §8 exactly.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the sheet, when reviewed, then every creature lists >= 1 avoid option and >= 1 trick or social option.
- AC-2 [content] Given the sheet, when reviewed, then every vulnerability is expressed as a property or stimulus (e.g. "frozen and fragile shatters"), with zero spell- or item-name pairings.
- AC-3 [content] Given the telegraph table, when reviewed, then every unblockable or grab move lists windup >= 500 ms and a distinct audio+VFX cue id.

items.title: Forgotten crumble and reassemble unless bones are scattered or burned
items.description:
## Why
Bible §8: the Forgotten crumble and reassemble — understanding that rule, and breaking it systemically, is the fight.

## What
As a player, I want downed skeletons to rise again unless I deal with their bones so that I learn to fight smart (scatter, burn, smash).
On Died, the skeleton becomes a bone-pile entity (physics, flammable after oil, fragile). After 8 s it reassembles if >= 60% of bones remain within 2 m. Blocked by: bones scattered by force/impulse, bones burning or burnt, crushing blunt hit on the pile, or holy water (tag consecrated). Animate Bones may claim a pile.

## Scope
- In: Bone-pile entity, reassembly timer and rules, property hooks
- Out: Animate Bones spell (e08-spell-animate-bones)

## Notes
Rules via properties only: impulse, burning, blunt impact, consecrated. Reassembly emits a telegraph (bones rattle, 1 s) so players can react.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a bone pile untouched, when 8 s pass, then the skeleton reassembles at 50% health with a 1 s telegraph beforehand.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a bone pile hit by an impulse that moves > 40% of bones beyond 2 m, when 8 s pass, then it does not reassemble and becomes inert.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a bone pile with burning = true for >= 2 s, when evaluated, then it becomes burnt and never reassembles, regardless of the heat source.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a pile reassembles while the player stands on it, when it completes, then the player is displaced safely with no clipping (edge).

items.title: Add monk Forgotten and habit routines that ignore quiet players
items.description:
## Why
The Forgotten are people who forgot themselves; they sweep, pray and haul — and can be avoided.

## What
As a thief, I want skeletons absorbed in old habits so that I can slip past, and as a player I want the monk variant to fight differently.
forgotten-monk (staff sweep, censer swing that carries live embers) plus habit routines as patrol data: sweeping, praying at altars, hauling buckets/ore. Habit trance: perception reduced 50% while performing a habit; noise above a threshold breaks it. Calmed by hymn-tagged noise (see e14-hum-vesper-hymn); hostile regardless at song intensity 3.

## Scope
- In: Monk variant data and moves, habit routine library, trance perception modifier, calm rule
- Out: Song-intensity state (e13-song-intensity)
- Out: Placement (E26)

## Notes
The censer is a heat source: it ignites flammable things it touches, including the monk's own oil-soaked surroundings. Related: e03-gas-clouds (P2) — if it lands, the censer may also leave a smoke cloud.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given forgotten-monk.json, when validated, then its moves pass readability and its censer move declares a heat stimulus via the stimulus API.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a sweeping Forgotten and a crouched player moving at walk speed 4 m behind it in dim light, when 10 s pass, then it stays Unaware.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a Forgotten in Combat, when a hymn-tagged noise reaches it at song intensity <= 2, then it drops to Unaware and resumes its habit within 3 s.
- AC-4 [integration] Given song intensity 3, when the hymn is heard, then the Forgotten ignores it and stays hostile (edge).

items.title: Drive creature behaviour from a global song-intensity world state
items.description:
## Why
The Nightjar's song is the dungeon's weather: when it swells, the Forgotten turn, Hushlings multiply and Clatter forgets.

## What
As a designer, I want one world fact song.intensity (0–3) that creature data can react to so that story beats reshape encounters without scripts.
Fact set by quest effects (e39-main-quest-data) and by events (sour bell ring = +1 for 5 minutes; Horn dead = +1 permanent). Creature data declares modifiers per intensity: aggression, perception, spawn weights, calm immunity.

## Scope
- In: Fact registration, timed modifiers, creature-data modifier hook, debug command
- Out: Which quest beats set it (E39)

## Notes
Also read by audio (music tension layer) — Related: e28-adaptive-music.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given intensity 1 and a +1 timed modifier for 300 s, when 300 s elapse, then intensity returns to 1 exactly once.
- AC-2 [unit] Given modifiers pushing intensity above 3, when evaluated, then it clamps to 3 (edge).
- AC-3 [integration] Given a Hushling spawner with weights per intensity, when intensity rises from 1 to 2, then spawn weights switch on the next spawner evaluation.

items.title: Add Rootcellar goblin combatants: slings, nets and loud alarms
items.description:
## Why
Goblins are clever scavengers, not fodder: they call for help, flee when outnumbered and can be talked to.

## What
As a player, I want goblins that fight like a clan (slings, nets, alarms, retreat) so that fighting them feels different from undead.
goblin-scavenger and goblin-slinger data: sling stone (ranged, 300 ms windup), net throw (grab-class, 500 ms, entangles 2 s, flammable), kettle-helm (head region blunt resistance 0.5, pierce deflect). Alarm pots and shouts via e11-communication. Morale: flee when allies are outnumbered 2:1. Immune to song and Hushling mimicry (they do not dream).

## Scope
- In: Two goblin variants, moves, head region armour, morale thresholds, alarm device entity
- Out: Talking, trade, capture-negotiation (E14)
- Out: Camp placement (e26-deepworks-encounters)

## Notes
Surrender intent (e11-retreat-flee) opens E14 negotiation.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given both goblin files, when validated, then the net throw declares a grab telegraph >= 30 ticks with distinct cue ids.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a goblin netted player, when any heat source touches the net, then the net burns off and the player is freed.
- AC-3 [integration] Given 3 goblins facing a player plus 2 allied creatures, when one goblin falls, then the rest flee toward the nearest alarm device.
- AC-4 [unit] Given song intensity 3, when goblin perception and aggression are evaluated, then they are unchanged (edge: goblins immune).

items.title: Add Loom Spiders that weave readable webs and fear bright light
items.description:
## Why
Loom spiders make the Outer Ring feel alive and teach "light and fire change the fight".

## What
As a player, I want pale dog-sized spiders that climb walls, web routes and flee bright light so that I can drive them off instead of fighting.
loom-spider: climber locomotion (walls/ceilings), bite (poison), web spit (slows 40% for 3 s, 300 ms windup). Places web entities (flammable, blocks passage, can carry copied rune text). Fear: light level >= 0.7 at its position triggers flee. Fire: burning = flee + damage.

## Scope
- In: Creature data, web entity prefab with readable text slot, fear-of-light rule
- Out: Web rune-clue puzzle placement (e26-knot-rune-navigation)

## Notes
Webs readable by any class with a light source; sorcerers with Hornfolk fragments read more (content in E26/E39).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given loom-spider.json, when validated, then it declares climber locomotion and a light-level fear threshold.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a spider in Combat, when the light level at its position rises to >= 0.7 from any source, then it flees to the darkest reachable point within 20 m.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a web in a doorway, when it ignites, then it burns away within 3 s and the doorway navmesh link opens.
- AC-4 [integration] Given no dark point is reachable, when fear triggers, then the spider cowers in place and its defence drops (edge).

items.title: Add silent Briar Wolf packs that can be fed, scared or remembered
items.description:
## Why
The wolves' silence is the first uncanny sign; a pack not fought should remember the player.

## What
As a player, I want a wolf pack that circles, flanks and can be fed or frightened so that the Briarwood has a living threat with options.
briar-wolf: fast walker, smell + hearing; bite, lunge (300 ms), flank coordination. Fear of fire (burning within 4 m). Feeding: meat items (edible:meat) thrown near the pack pacify for 120 s and raise pack disposition. Pack memory world fact (wolves.fed, wolves.harmed) persists and changes greeting behaviour. Sleepwalkers are ignored (song stills animals).

## Scope
- In: Wolf data, pack coordination tags, feeding rule, fear rule, pack-memory facts
- Out: Den placement (e25-wolf-den)

## Notes
Silent: wolves have no howl cue while the breach is open; add a howl variant for the "Vespers Rung" ending state.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a pack Suspicious of the player, when an edible:meat item lands within 5 m, then the pack eats and stays non-hostile for 120 s.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a burning object within 4 m of a wolf, when evaluated, then the wolf backs away and will not path through the fire.
- AC-3 [integration] Given fact wolves.fed >= 2, when the player next enters the den, then the pack starts at disposition Wary instead of Hostile.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a sleepwalking NPC passes through the pack, when perceived, then no wolf targets the NPC (edge).

items.title: Add blind Hushlings that hunt by sound and break at loud noises
items.description:
## Why
Hushlings are the thief's nightmare and playground: silence is survival, loudness is a weapon.

## What
As a thief, I want blind fog-children that hunt purely by sound so that silence and distraction are my tools; as a knight, I want to learn that my clanking draws them.
hushling: sight disabled, hearing only, drifts; grasp attack (500 ms, unblockable, distinct whisper cue). Mimic barks using the names of the missing ("Da? I'm cold"). Any noise event with loudness >= 0.85 within 6 m tears them apart (dissipate). Ignore goblins.

## Scope
- In: Creature data with hearing-only senses, loud-noise dissipation rule, mimic bark set ids
- Out: Bark text (e39-item-creature-text)
- Out: Placement (E25/E26)

## Notes
Loud sources include bells, Thunderclap, shattered glass, shield bash on metal — all via noise loudness, never pairings.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a crouched player moving silently in full light within 3 m, when 10 s pass, then the Hushling does not detect them (sight disabled).
- AC-2 [integration] Given a noise event of loudness >= 0.85 within 6 m, when propagated, then every Hushling in range dissipates.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a thrown distraction at 8 m, when heard, then the Hushling investigates the noise location, not the player.
- AC-4 [content] Given the grasp attack, when validated, then it is unblockable with windup >= 30 ticks and a unique audio cue (edge: readability for a blind hunter).

items.title: Add Tallow Ooze that melts into fire puddles and shatters when frozen
items.description:
## Why
The ooze is a systemic toy: the best way to fight it is with the world's properties.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want a slow wax slime that reacts to heat and cold so that experimenting pays off.
tallow-ooze: slow, sticky engulf (slows 50%), splits into two small oozes on heavy blunt hits. Heat: melts into a spreading flammable puddle (flammable liquid volume) that can then be ignited. Cold: frozen + fragile → shatters on impact.

## Scope
- In: Creature data, split rule, melt-to-puddle and freeze-to-brittle property rules
- Out: Scriptorium placement (e26-priory-scriptorium)

## Notes
Puddle cap: max 6 active puddles per room to protect the element-field budget.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given an ooze exposed to heat above its melt threshold for 2 s, when evaluated, then it becomes a flammable puddle entity covering >= 2 m².
- AC-2 [integration] Given an ooze with frozen = true, when any impact >= its fragile threshold hits it, then it shatters and dies.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a heavy blunt hit on a full-size ooze, when resolved, then two half-size oozes spawn; half-size oozes do not split again (edge).

items.title: Add book, lectern and chest mimics with tells and feeding
items.description:
## Why
Mimics reward curiosity and observation: a careful player spots the tell; a clever one feeds them.

## What
As a player, I want mimics disguised as books, lecterns and chests that I can spot, feed, avoid or wake so that containers stay exciting.
Three variants (book-mimic, lectern-mimic, chest-mimic) presenting as interactables. Tell: subtle breathing motion + faint paper-rustle noise audible within 3 m. Bite on interact (500 ms, grab-class). Feeding: any item tagged edible:paper placed on/near it pacifies and yields a treat item.

## Scope
- In: Three variants, disguise-as-interactable hook, tell cues, feed rule, drop tables
- Out: Mortimer the tame mimic (e14-mortimer)

## Notes
Waking on purpose (strike first) is valid; mimic then fights normally but flees at 30% health.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a disguised chest-mimic, when the player interacts, then a 500 ms telegraph plays before the bite and a dodge in that window avoids it.
- AC-2 [integration] Given an edible:paper item placed within 1 m, when 3 s pass, then the mimic eats it, becomes pacified and drops its treat.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player listens within 3 m, when the tell noise plays, then it is captioned by the sound-caption system when captions are enabled (edge).

items.title: Add Hollow Sentinels bound to hold the tower until relieved
items.description:
## Why
The Sentinels embody "keeping watch": honour-bound, relentless inside the tower, and able to be relieved rather than destroyed.

## What
As a knight, I want armour that obeys a forty-year-old order so that speaking the old words ends the fight honourably.
hollow-sentinel: slow walker, sight + life-sense, never sleeps; halberd sweep, shield charge (500 ms, unblockable). Leash: never leaves the tower volume. Resistances pierce 0.3, blunt 1.5, conductive. Stand-down conditions (facts): watchword spoken, knight formal relief, "watch ended" bell rung, binding dispelled. Stood-down sentinels salute and fall still permanently.

## Scope
- In: Creature data, leash volume, stand-down fact conditions, salute state
- Out: Dialogue lines for watchword and relief (e39-side-quests-wilds)
- Out: Tower placement (e25-mooring-watch-encounters)

## Notes
Smashing them is valid but slow (high poise). Dispel uses a generic magic-binding property so any dispel-capable effect works.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a sentinel in Combat, when the player leaves the tower volume, then it returns to its stand and does not path outside.
- AC-2 [integration] Given fact watch.ended is set, when evaluated, then all sentinels salute and become inert within 3 s and stay inert after save/reload.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a pierce hit of 40, when resolved, then 12 damage applies; given a blunt 40, then 60 (edge: armour identity).
- AC-4 [integration] Given a sentinel standing in water and a shock stimulus, when propagated, then it is staggered via conductivity.

items.title: Add Brother Horn's creature data: charges, grabs and throws to stop
items.description:
## Why
Horn fights to stop, not to kill — his combat must say so.

## What
As a player, I want the minotaur to fight like a warden restraining an intruder so that the fight hints he is not a monster.
npc-horn creature: 9 ft, walker; moves: axe sweep (parryable), charge (unblockable, 600 ms, bellow cue), grab-and-throw (grab-class, 500 ms), stomp (ground AoE). Non-lethal rule: damage from Horn cannot reduce the player below 1 HP; at <= 15% HP his next hit subdues (player.subdued event, not Died), routed to the Fold via e01-contextual-respawn.

## Scope
- In: Creature data, move set, non-lethal clamp, subdue event
- Out: Encounter phases, yield and trial (e13-horn-encounter)
- Out: Befriend/help (e14-horn-befriend-help)

## Notes
Horn is also a social creature — the same entity is shared with E14.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given npc-horn.json, when validated, then the charge and grab moves are unblockable/grab with windups >= 30 ticks and distinct cues.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the player at 10 HP, when a Horn hit of 50 resolves, then the player ends at 1 HP and no Died event fires.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player at <= 15% HP, when Horn's next hit lands, then player.subdued fires and the respawn resolver routes to the Fold.
- AC-4 [integration] Given environmental damage (a fall) while fighting Horn, when it would kill the player, then normal death applies (edge: clamp only on Horn's own hits).

items.title: Build the Warden boss encounter with yield, spare and Trial of Horns
items.description:
## Why
The Warden encounter is the pivotal moment of the game (bible §4.2); combat must feed every resolution.

## What
As a player, I want the Horn fight to end in a choice so that combat becomes a story decision.
Phases: guarding (circles, warns), fighting, yielding at 20% HP ("Enough. Hear me, or finish it.") — combat pauses; the player must explicitly attack again to kill (fact horn.killed) or lower weapon/interact to spare (horn.spared, wounded). Trial of Horns mode (knight capability): no-kill honour duel; first to three clean parries/blocks wins (horn.befriended via trial). Portcullis-trapped state and "rests one eye" state as encounter states for trick resolutions.

## Scope
- In: Encounter state machine, yield/kill/spare gating, trial rules and counter, trick states exposed as facts
- Out: Horn's Hall level (e26-horns-hall-fold)
- Out: Dialogue (e39-dialogue-horn)

## Notes
Killing requires an explicit second action after the yield (e39-main-quest-data note).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given Horn at 20% HP, when the threshold is crossed, then he yields, all his attacks stop and horn.yielded is set.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a yielded Horn, when the player lands a deliberate attack, then horn.killed is set and his horn item drops; when the player interacts instead, then horn.spared is set.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the Trial of Horns, when the knight lands 3 clean parries/blocks before taking 3 clean hits, then the trial is won, horn.befriended is set and no damage below 1 HP ever applies.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the player loses the trial, when resolved, then Horn offers a rematch and the encounter does not become lethal (edge).

items.title: Add the Sleepless Abbot wraith: solid only while singing
items.description:
## Why
The abbot must be beatable by understanding him — sound and light break his concentration — not by damage race.

## What
As a player, I want a wraith who is only vulnerable while singing and whose form is anchored to lanterns so that I defeat him with observation.
npc-abbot creature: fog body; states singing (solid, damageable, commands Hushlings) and drifting (immune). Loud noise (>= 0.85) or bright light (>= 0.9) within 5 m interrupts singing and staggers. Anchor lanterns: 4 linked lantern entities; each destroyed/extinguished removes 25% of his max health. Summons Hushlings while singing (cap 4).

## Scope
- In: Creature data, sing/drift state rules, anchor link component, summon cap
- Out: Cradle encounter and resolutions (e13-abbot-encounter)

## Notes
Interrupt rules by stimulus threshold only — bell, Thunderclap, shattered glass, Wisp Light all qualify systemically.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the abbot drifting, when any damage packet hits, then 0 damage applies and immune feedback shows.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the abbot singing, when a noise >= 0.85 occurs within 5 m, then singing is interrupted, he is staggered for 2 s and becomes damageable during it.
- AC-3 [integration] Given two of four anchor lanterns extinguished, when his max health is read, then it is 50% of base.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the Hushling cap of 4 is reached, when he sings again, then no further Hushlings spawn (edge).

items.title: Build the Cradle encounter with fight, trick, persuade and join paths
items.description:
## Why
The final confrontation must honour every class and the persuade path earned through Clatter.

## What
As a player, I want to end the abbot by fighting, tricking, persuading or joining him so that my choices and class matter at the climax.
Fight: via e13-abbot-wraith rules. Trick: pickpocket the tongue from his belt while singing (thief; sets tongue.recovered); a Mirror Self decoy emitting hymn-tagged noise turns nearby Forgotten on him; shooting anchor lanterns. Persuade: available only if clatter.restored and Clatter present. Join: dialogue choice → ending 4 state. Tansy-hostage variant if tansy.reachedCradle.

## Scope
- In: Encounter state machine, trick hooks (pickpocket target, faction flip on hymn), hostage variant, outcome facts
- Out: Cradle level (e26-cradle-arena)
- Out: Abbot dialogue (e39-dialogue-abbot)

## Notes
Pickpocketing the tongue is "the single most satisfying theft in the game" — give it a 1.5 s pickpocket window during each sing phase.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the abbot singing and the thief behind him, when pickpocket succeeds, then tongue.recovered is set and the abbot enters a fury phase.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a hymn-tagged noise from any source during the fight, when Forgotten are within 10 m, then they switch faction target to the abbot for 20 s.
- AC-3 [integration] Given clatter.restored is false, when the persuade option is evaluated, then it is not offered; given true with Clatter present, then it is.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the Tansy-hostage variant, when an area attack would hit Tansy, then she is protected (no damage) and the abbot moves her (edge).

items.title: Author the MVP creature faction and relationship table
items.description:
## Why
Creatures have relationships; setting them against each other is a valid solution.

## What
As a designer, I want a faction table for the MVP roster so that goblins fight spiders, Hushlings ignore goblins and players can exploit it.
Factions: forgotten, rootcellar, warden, loom, briar-pack, dream (Hushlings + abbot), sentinels, mimic, ooze. Relationships: rootcellar ↔ loom hostile; dream ignores rootcellar; briar-pack avoids mine volumes; forgotten neutral to dream until intensity 3; warden protective of sleepers.

## Scope
- In: Faction data, relationship matrix, content tests
- Out: Faction runtime (e12-factions-relationships)

## Notes
Player standing with factions is disposition (E14/E22), not this table.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the faction table, when validated, then every MVP creature references exactly one existing faction.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a goblin and a loom spider in mutual sight, when perceived, then they enter Combat with each other.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a Hushling and a goblin within 2 m, when evaluated, then neither targets the other (edge).

items.title: Gate CI on creature readability, avoidability and arena smoke tests
items.description:
## Why
Readable telegraphs and non-combat options are constitutional; they must not rot as creatures are tuned.

## What
A CI audit over all shipping creature data: every attack passes the readability rule; every creature declares >= 1 avoid option and has a scenario test proving it; every declared vulnerability has a property-based test; a 12-creature mixed Ossuary scene runs in the perf suite.

## Scope
- In: Audit script and report (docs/design/bestiary-audit.md), scenario tests, perf scene
- Out: Framework-level harness (e12-creature-content-harness)

## Notes
Reuse e32-combat-stress-scene infrastructure for the perf scene.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a creature move with a 12-tick windup, when the audit runs, then CI fails naming the creature and move.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a creature with no avoid-option scenario test, when the audit runs, then CI fails (edge).
- AC-3 [perf] Given 8 Forgotten, 2 Hushlings and 2 loom spiders active with fire, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent) and p95 <= 16.7 ms at 1080p on the Low preset on an Intel Iris Xe / base M1 8 GB class machine, with p99 <= 33.3 ms (30 fps floor) during worst-case combat.

items.title: Tune the bestiary from creature-arena sessions and playtest telemetry
items.description:
## Why
Creatures should be memorable for behaviour; tuning must be evidence-led.

## What
Run creature-arena sessions per class against every MVP creature and read playtest telemetry (deaths, abandon points). Adjust timings, health, perception within design bounds; record changes in docs/design/bestiary-tuning.md.

## Scope
- In: Arena sessions, telemetry review, data tuning PR, tuning log
- Out: Framework changes (file beads in E11/E12)

## Notes
Related: e34-analysis-scripts, e35-external-round-1.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given one tester per class, when each fights every creature once, then median time-to-kill for regular creatures is between 15 s and 60 s.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the tuned data, when the bestiary audit runs, then it still passes (tuning never breaks readability).
- AC-3 [content] Given the tuning log, when reviewed, then each change cites the observation or telemetry metric that motivated it.

items.title: Let the player hum the Vesper hymn after reading the Vesperine Hours
items.description:
## Why
Humming the hymn calms the Forgotten, befriends Horn and rewards reading — a verb every class can learn from a book.

## What
As a player of any class, I want to learn the Vesper hymn from The Vesperine Hours and hum it so that I can calm the dead and speak to the warden.
Reading the hymn page grants capability verb.hum.vesper-hymn. Hum is a held action: emits a noise event every 0.5 s tagged hymn (loudness 0.3), movement slowed to walk. Creatures declare responses in data (calmedBy: hymn).

## Scope
- In: Capability grant on read, hum action and animation hook, hymn-tagged noise emission
- Out: The book item and shop placement (e24-lamplit-stacks)
- Out: Creature responses (E13/E14 creature items)

## Notes
Mirror Self can emit hymn-tagged noise via the same tag (Cradle trick). Humming while sneaking still makes noise — a real trade-off.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the player reads the hymn page, when complete, then verb.hum.vesper-hymn is granted with source book:vesperine-hours.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the player humming for 2 s, when noise events are inspected, then 4 events tagged hymn with loudness 0.3 are emitted.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player without the capability, when the hum action is pressed, then nothing is emitted and no prompt shows (edge).

items.title: Make the Rootcellar clan talkable, bribable and forgiving of capture
items.description:
## Why
"A goblin camp might actually have people to talk to." Getting caught should open negotiation, not end the game.

## What
As a player, I want to approach the goblin camp as a guest, a trader or a trespasser so that my approach changes how the clan treats me.
Clan disposition (faction-level) with modifiers: gifts of shiny/kettle items, returning salvage, harming goblins, freeing Duggan by force. Guests: goblins stay Wary, trade allowed. Capture: when the player is netted/subdued in the camp, they are dragged to Kettleback (fact goblins.capturedPlayer) and dialogue opens regardless of prior hostility. Thieves get a kin bonus.

## Scope
- In: Clan disposition rules, gift preferences, capture-to-negotiation flow, kin bonus
- Out: Kettleback and Snig specifics (e14-mother-kettleback, e14-snig)
- Out: Dialogue text (e39-dialogue-labyrinth-folk)

## Notes
Clan standing is one of the ending facts (goblin standing).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given clan disposition Neutral and a gift tagged kettle, when given, then disposition rises by the gift preference value and a goblins.gifted fact increments.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the player is subdued inside the camp volume, when the subdue resolves, then the player wakes in front of Kettleback and her dialogue starts.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player killed >= 3 goblins, when entering the camp, then goblins start Alerted but capture still leads to negotiation (edge).
- AC-4 [unit] Given the thief class, when clan disposition is initialised, then it starts one band higher than for other classes.

items.title: Bring Mother Kettleback to life: trade, Duggan crate and carrying fees
items.description:
## Why
Kettleback is a memorable monster-character: pragmatic, sarcastic and useful.

## What
As a player, I want to bargain with the goblin matriarch so that I can trade, free Duggan Marl and hire her clan.
npc-kettleback: creature + merchant (goblin salvage stock), gift likes (kettles, brass, shiny), Duggan crate interaction states (trade for Dot's kettle, persuade to release, force), clan hire effects (wall the breach, hold the shaft), and the carrying-fee rule when she retrieves a dead player (post-Horn-death).

## Scope
- In: Creature/merchant data, gift table, Duggan crate state entity, hire effects as facts, carrying fee rule
- Out: Framed in Brass quest graph (e39-side-quests-wilds)

## Notes
Kettleback never fights unless the camp is attacked; she flees to the back tunnel at 50% health.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given npc-kettleback.json and her merchant data, when validated, then both pass and stock references existing items.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the player gives Dot's kettle, when accepted, then duggan.released is set and the crate opens.
- AC-3 [integration] Given clan disposition Friendly and a hire request, when accepted, then goblins.hired.breach is set for the breach-sealing option.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the player attacks Kettleback, when her health reaches 50%, then she flees via the back tunnel and the clan becomes Hostile (edge).

items.title: Bring Snig to life: pocket-picking, reading lessons and vouching
items.description:
## Why
Snig is the game's comic heart and the goblin who wants to read.

## What
As a player, I want Snig to steal from me, follow me and vouch for me so that he becomes a recurring ally.
npc-snig: attempts to pickpocket the player (thief can notice and allow — snig.trusted); Bookshop Burglar outcomes as facts (jailed, lessons, scared of the reading one); follower mode in town and mine; vouch flag used by Horn befriend; fear of Mortimer (flees if within 5 m).

## Scope
- In: Creature data, pickpocket-the-player behaviour, follower mode, outcome facts
- Out: Bookshop Burglar quest graph (e39-side-quests-town)

## Notes
If jailed, the thief can bust him out through the jail drain (e24-watch-house-jail).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given Snig adjacent and the player idle, when his pickpocket attempt succeeds, then one low-value item moves to his inventory and the thief class receives a notice prompt.
- AC-2 [integration] Given snig.lessons is set, when Horn's befriend conditions are evaluated, then the vouch option is available.
- AC-3 [integration] Given Mortimer within 5 m of Snig, when evaluated, then Snig flees and follower mode pauses until distance > 10 m (edge).

items.title: Build Clatter: the apologetic skeleton who can remember his name
items.description:
## Why
"A skeleton might remember fragments of its previous life." Clatter is the warmest quest in the game.

## What
As a player, I want a skeleton that apologises while fighting, calms to the hymn and regains memories so that helping him feels like the heart of the story.
npc-clatter: Forgotten variant; hostile-apologetic (reduced aggression, apology barks) unless hymn heard; tends mushroom garden idle. Memory pieces as facts (psalter, pear-bloom, sister's letter); song intensity 3 removes the most recent unanchored memory. Sorcerer memory-reading: success skips a piece; failure removes one permanently. Outcomes: clatter.restored → follower to Cradle; or rest (knight rites / psalter on priory altar).

## Scope
- In: Creature data, memory facts and loss rule, reading attempt check, follower/rest outcomes
- Out: Name on the Bones quest graph (e39-side-quests-wilds)
- Out: Clatter dialogue (e39-dialogue-labyrinth-folk)

## Notes
Clatter must never be killable by accident while calm: friendly-fire off when disposition >= Friendly.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given Clatter hostile, when a hymn-tagged noise reaches him, then he stops attacking and opens dialogue.
- AC-2 [unit] Given 2 memories recovered and song intensity rising to 3, when evaluated, then the most recent memory not yet anchored is removed and the fact is cleared.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a failed memory-reading attempt, when resolved, then one memory is permanently lost and cannot be recovered by its piece (edge).
- AC-4 [integration] Given clatter.restored, when the player enters the Cradle, then Clatter follows and is present for the persuade option.

items.title: Befriend and help Brother Horn without fighting
items.description:
## Why
"A minotaur guarding an ancient labyrinth might be fought, tricked, befriended or helped."

## What
As a player, I want to lower my weapon, hum, return his mother's horn-ring or have friends vouch so that Horn becomes my ally.
Befriend triggers: player sheathed and stationary for 6 s in Horn's sight (he circles three times, then speaks); hymn heard; horn-ring or the Hornfolk name-stone (from The Crate for Mr. S—, e40-crate-heist) given; vouch (snig.lessons or clatter present). Help steps: bread for sleepers, healing (salve, Nature spell, rest in Fold), breach sealed. Ally mode: follows to key points, opens the crypt shortcut, holds the shaft foot in the climb.

## Scope
- In: Befriend trigger rules, help-step facts, ally behaviours (open crypt, hold shaft)
- Out: Horn dialogue (e39-dialogue-horn)
- Out: Combat encounter (e13-horn-encounter)

## Notes
Befriend is combinable with spared/tricked outcomes (bible §4.2).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the player sheathed and stationary for 6 s in Horn's sight, when evaluated, then Horn circles the player 3 times and opens dialogue instead of attacking.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the player draws a weapon during the circling, when detected, then the befriend attempt aborts and Horn resumes guarding (edge).
- AC-3 [integration] Given horn.befriended and the player at the crypt door, when Horn is asked, then the crypt shortcut opens and shortcut.crypt is set permanently.
- AC-4 [integration] Given horn.befriended and horn.healed, when the climb begins, then Horn holds the shaft foot and Hushlings target him first.

items.title: Add Mortimer, the tame book mimic who guards the rare shelf
items.description:
## Why
Mortimer makes the bookshop memorable and makes shoplifting a story rather than a menu.

## What
As a player, I want Mirela's tame mimic to bite shoplifters and be won over with paper so that the bookshop has a guardian with personality.
npc-mortimer: stationary mimic on the rare shelf; detects witnessed theft from the shop (e27-ownership-theft) within 6 m and bites (non-lethal); sets mirela.banned for 1 in-game day; bringing biscuits to Mirela lifts it early; can be fed paper for a treat (Mortimer's tooth rare drop if provoked).

## Scope
- In: Creature data, theft-detect-and-bite rule, ban fact with timeout, feed rule
- Out: Bookshop stock (e24-lamplit-stacks)
- Out: Snig-meets-Mortimer beat (e39-side-quests-town)

## Notes
Mortimer never leaves his shelf; theft from other shelves out of his view is not detected by him.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the player takes an owned book within Mortimer's view, when theft is recorded, then Mortimer bites for non-lethal damage and mirela.banned is set.
- AC-2 [unit] Given mirela.banned set at day 3 08:00, when world time reaches day 4 08:00, then the ban clears.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a theft outside Mortimer's view, when recorded, then Mortimer does not react (edge).

items.title: Prove every social creature path in an automated scenario suite
items.description:
## Why
Social paths are easy to break silently; every one must stay reachable.

## What
Scenario tests (e11-ai-scenario-harness + quest/dialogue test runners) for each P1 path: goblins guest/trade/capture; Kettleback Duggan trade/persuade/force; Clatter hymn/memories/loss/restore/rest; Horn wait/hymn/ring/vouch/trial/help. The suite is a registry: Snig and Mortimer (P2) register their own scenarios in their items.

## Scope
- In: Scenario suite, CI job, coverage report of social paths
- Out: Quest-level validation (e23-quest-validator)

## Notes
Report lists each path id and its outcome fact. Related: e14-snig, e14-mortimer add scenarios to this registry when they land.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the suite, when run in CI, then every path listed in docs/design/bestiary.md social options reaches its outcome fact.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a path whose outcome fact is never set, when the suite runs, then CI fails naming the path (edge).
- AC-3 [integration] Given each social failure path (capture, ban, lost memory), when run, then the resulting state offers at least one further action (no dead end).

items.title: Write the MVP obstacle × class route matrix
items.description:
## Why
Classes change possibilities; level designers need one table of every mandatory obstacle and its intended class routes before blockout.

## What
docs/design/route-matrix.md: every mandatory obstacle on the critical path (mine gate, supply tunnel, goblin camp passage, Outer Ring gate, Ossuary crossing, Chapel, Horn's Hall/Fold access, Cradle, Sounding Shaft, belfry) the six mine entries including the Weeping Adit, and major optional ones (Vane House strongbox, Mooring's Watch, restricted shelf, and Wendmouth's customs strongroom, bay nine, the Gilded Tern and the Undertow — mandatory within their quests) × knight/archer/sorcerer/thief/any, naming capabilities used and the source of each route in the story bible §4.3.

## Scope
- In: Matrix document, obstacle ids (kebab-case) reused by the registry
- Out: Registry data (e16-obstacle-registry)
- Out: Puzzle solution coverage (e15-solution-audit)

## Notes
Obstacles vs puzzles: puzzles are audited by e15; obstacles here are traversal/infiltration/encounter gates.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the matrix, when reviewed, then every mandatory obstacle lists >= 3 class routes and at least one "any class" route or fallback.
- AC-2 [content] Given the matrix, when reviewed, then every route names capability ids that exist in the e19 capability data or are flagged "needs capability" with an owning epic.
- AC-3 [content] Given obstacles with only 2 class routes, when found, then each is listed in a "gaps" section with a proposed fix (edge).

items.title: Declare obstacles and class routes as validated content data
items.description:
## Why
Routes must be data so they can be audited and replayed, not tribal knowledge.

## What
Schema content/obstacles/*.json: {id, scene, mandatory, routes: [{id, classes, requiredCapabilities, entities (ids of the anchor points, weak walls, vents…), replay?}]} with a validator that checks scene/entity/capability references.

## Scope
- In: Zod schema, validator, entries for every matrix obstacle
- Out: Audit gate (e16-route-audit)

## Notes
Entities referenced must carry the property that makes the route work (e.g. climbable, weakened, shootable) — the validator checks the property exists.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given an obstacle entry, when validated, then every referenced scene, entity and capability id exists.
- AC-2 [content] Given a route referencing a weak wall entity lacking the weakened property, when validated, then validation fails (edge).
- AC-3 [content] Given the registry, when compared to the route matrix, then every matrix obstacle id has an entry.

items.title: Fail CI when a mandatory obstacle lacks three class routes
items.description:
## Why
"Problems support multiple solutions" must be enforced, not hoped for.

## What
CI audit reusing e15-solution-audit class capability profiles: for each obstacle, evaluate each route against each class's MVP capability profile; fail if a mandatory obstacle has < 3 classes with a valid route. Generates docs/design/route-coverage.md and a PR diff summary.

## Scope
- In: Audit script, CI gate, generated report
- Out: Puzzle audits (e15-solution-audit)

## Notes
Shares profile data with e15; do not duplicate profiles.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a mandatory obstacle with valid routes for only knight and thief, when CI runs, then it fails naming the obstacle and the missing classes.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a route requiring a capability absent from every class profile, when audited, then the route is reported invalid (edge).
- AC-3 [integration] Given all obstacles pass, when CI runs, then the report is regenerated and the PR summary lists coverage deltas versus main.

items.title: Replay every declared class route to prove it is traversable
items.description:
## Why
A declared route that does not actually work is worse than none.

## What
Each route in the registry gets a short recorded replay (from a start marker to the obstacle's exit fact) run headlessly in CI; failing replays mark the route invalid in the audit.

## Scope
- In: Replays per route, runner, audit integration
- Out: Full critical-path replays (e26-dungeon-playtest)

## Notes
Replays start from committed save fixtures near each obstacle to stay short. Related: e33-teleport-bookmarks (P2) can generate those fixtures faster if it lands.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given each declared route, when its replay runs, then the obstacle exit fact is set.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a replay that fails, when the audit runs, then that route no longer counts toward coverage.
- AC-3 [integration] Given level geometry changes that break a replay, when CI runs, then the failure names the obstacle, route and first diverging checkpoint (edge).

items.title: Close class-route gaps in Briar Glen, the wilds and Wendmouth
items.description:
## Why
The audit will find gaps; closing them is authoring work with a clear owner.

## What
As a player of any class, I want every surface obstacle to have my class's route so that I never feel my class was forgotten.
