For every E24/E25/E40 obstacle flagged by the audit: add anchor points, weak walls, climbable ivy, vents, shootable counterweights or spell affordances until >= 3 (target 4) classes pass.

## Scope
- In: Level data edits in town and wilderness scenes, registry updates, replays
- Out: Dungeon gaps (e16-gap-pass-dungeon)

## Notes
Prefer adding a route over widening an existing one.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the audit after this pass, when run, then every E24/E25/E40 mandatory obstacle passes with >= 3 classes.
- AC-2 [integration] Given each newly added route, when replayed, then it passes.
- AC-3 [perf] Given the added props, when the town and Briarwood perf scenes run, then budgets from the hardware baseline still hold (edge: no perf regression).

items.title: Close class-route gaps in the Deepworks, priory and the Knot
items.description:
## Why
The dungeon is the constitution's showcase: "the knight forces, the thief infiltrates, the archer manipulates, the sorcerer alters."

## What
As a player of any class, I want every dungeon obstacle to have my class's route so that the Labyrinth plays differently for me.
For every E26 obstacle flagged by the audit: add routes until >= 3 (target 4) classes pass, preferring routes that express the class fantasy lines in the constitution MVP scenario.

## Scope
- In: Dungeon level data edits, registry updates, replays
- Out: Puzzle solutions (E15 audit)

## Notes
Target: all 4 classes for the mine gate, Horn's Hall and the Cradle.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the audit after this pass, when run, then every E26 mandatory obstacle passes with >= 3 classes and the mine gate, Horn's Hall and Cradle pass with 4.
- AC-2 [integration] Given each newly added route, when replayed, then it passes.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a route that consumes a one-shot resource (e.g. breaking the only weak wall), when used, then the obstacle stays passable for the remaining classes (edge).

items.title: Playtest the MVP critical path once per class for route fantasy
items.description:
## Why
Only players can tell whether a route feels like their class or like a checkbox.

## What
One tester per class plays the MVP critical path; observers log each obstacle, the route taken and whether the tester found their class route unprompted. Findings to docs/playtests/class-routes.md with beads.

## Scope
- In: 4 sessions, observation sheet, findings, beads
- Out: External playtests (e35-external-round-1)

## Notes
Run with builds from e35-playtest-builds.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [manual] Given each class tester, when they finish, then they found their class route unprompted at >= 60% of mandatory obstacles.
- AC-2 [manual] Given each tester, when surveyed, then they name >= 3 "wait, I can do that?" moments.
- AC-3 [content] Given the findings doc, when complete, then every obstacle where the class route was missed has a bead or an explicit "accepted" note (edge).

items.title: Design the world map: areas, loops, shortcuts and ability gates
items.description:
## Why
"Small world with surprising density": paths loop together and reveal shortcuts as players acquire abilities. Every level item needs this map first.

## What
docs/design/world-map.md plus content/world/connectivity.json: nodes (town districts, Briarwood zones, Mooring's Watch, mine gate, Deepworks zones, priory rooms, Knot areas) and edges {from, to, kind: path|door|shortcut|one-way|secret, unlock: condition, classesHint}. Loops from bible §3.1: forest ↔ watchtower ↔ priory; watchtower supply tunnel ↔ upper mine; priory crypt/Sounding Shaft ↔ Knot; Glen Well ↔ cistern ↔ priory; jail drain ↔ cistern; river loops — Weeping Adit ↔ lower Deepworks, Ore Stair (sorting hall → quay, one-way), Millweir sluice walk ↔ Briarwood far bank; the towpath (always open) and the barge (mornings) link Briar Glen Quay ↔ Kestrel Lock ↔ Wendmouth. Includes a validator: every node reachable from the town spawn with base class capabilities; every shortcut's unlock references a real fact.

## Scope
- In: Map doc with diagram, connectivity data, reachability validator
- Out: Scene transitions implementation (e01-area-transitions)

## Notes
Mine decision: Deepworks interior is E26; E25 owns the gate exterior and the tower tunnel up to the collapse. Time-gated edges read the e27-world-clock phase.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given connectivity.json, when validated, then every node is reachable from the town spawn using only edges with no unlock condition or unlocks available to all four base classes.
- AC-2 [content] Given every shortcut edge, when validated, then its unlock condition references a fact produced by some placed content (warning if unproduced).
- AC-3 [content] Given the doc, when reviewed, then it lists every land and river loop from bible §3.1, the barge/towpath link to Wendmouth, and at least one ability-gated shortcut per class.
- AC-4 [content] Given an edge referencing an unknown node, when validated, then validation fails naming it (edge).
- AC-5 [content] Given connectivity.json, when the main-quest critical path is computed, then it never requires a Wendmouth or barge edge (Wendmouth is optional).

items.title: Block out Briar Glen in grey-box with every named building shell
items.description:
## Why
Density before breadth: the town's layout decides sightlines, rooftops and schedules for everything after.

## What
As a player, I want to walk a compact valley town with recognisable landmarks so that I learn it within one visit.
Grey-box town (~180×140 m): mountain road entry, Market Green with notice board, the Sleeping Ox, Lamplit Stacks leaning on Brand's Forge, Fenn's Fletchery & Simples, Pell's Bakery, Watch House, Vane House on the rise, schoolhouse, Glen Well, lychgate cemetery; exits to Briarwood, mine road and priory road. Enterable shells with door transitions.

## Scope
- In: Town scene, building shells with doors, navmesh, exits wired to connectivity nodes, landmark sightlines
- Out: Interiors (per-building items)
- Out: Rooftop routes (e24-rooftops-thief-routes)

## Notes
Vane House visible from everywhere (it sits above the town — the power geography). The Stacks is three storeys and visibly leans.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the town scene, when validated, then every bible §3.5 town location has a named node and an entry transition or interactable.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the navmesh, when queried, then every building door is reachable from the road entry.
- AC-3 [e2e] Given the town tour replay, when run, then it visits each landmark and exits to Briarwood, mine road and priory road.
- AC-4 [perf] Given the grey-box town from Market Green, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).

items.title: Place systemic objects and hiding spots throughout Briar Glen
items.description:
## Why
The town must be a toybox too: lanterns to snuff, hay to hide in, troughs to freeze, washing lines to burn.

## What
As a player, I want the town full of things that react to fire, water, light and force so that I can improvise.
Lamp posts and window lights (extinguishable, relit by the lamplighter on schedule), water troughs, hay carts and barrels (hiding places), washing lines (flammable ropes), stacked crates, market stalls (breakable), shadowed alleys, loose cobbles for throwing.

## Scope
- In: Prop placement with material presets, hiding-place volumes, light sources, throwables
- Out: Interiors' props (per-building items)

## Notes
Fire in town is a real risk: flammable density near the Ox and stalls must be capped so fires burn out, not destroy the town (bible tone).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the town scene, when validated, then every placed prop uses an e03 material preset and no ad-hoc properties.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a fire started at a market stall, when simulated 120 s, then it burns out without spreading to building shells flagged non-flammable (edge).
- AC-3 [integration] Given a hay cart hiding place at night, when a guard passes at 3 m, then the hidden player remains undetected.

items.title: Build the Sleeping Ox inn: common room, rooms, cellar and rest
items.description:
## Why
The inn is the story's first night, the rumour hub and the Briarwood wake point.

## What
As a player, I want a warm inn where I can rest, hear rumours and sell hot goods so that town has a home base.
Interior: common room with hearth (Dot's Ember request can fail and scorch), bar, lending shelf, stairs to the player's room (the first-night window), Dot's back room (thief), cellar with fencing stock and the goblin kettle for Framed in Brass. Rest via an inn-kind rest point. Respawn rule: Briarwood deaths wake here.

## Scope
- In: Interior scene, inn-kind rest point (e27-rest-points) paid via e20-services, lending shelf books, cellar with fence merchant data, kettle item, respawn rule entry
- Out: Dot's dialogue (e39-dialogue-town-core)
- Out: Fence runtime (e20-fences-stolen-goods)

## Notes
Lending shelf books from e39-books-lore (A Traveller's Account of the Glen, The Ox Beneath the Hill copy).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the player rents the room, when resting until dawn, then rest.completed fires, the clock reads 06:00 and rest-reset facts reset.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the player dies in the Briarwood, when the respawn rule resolves, then the player wakes in the Ox room.
- AC-3 [content] Given Dot's fence merchant, when validated, then isFence is true and the goblin kettle is present in the cellar.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a botched Ember at the hearth, when fire spreads to the rug, then it is extinguishable and sets fact ox.scorched which Dot remarks on (edge).

items.title: Author the Lamplit Stacks bookshop on the e21 authoring template
items.description:
## Why
The constitution makes bookshops "genuinely exciting destinations"; this is the MVP's one excellent bookshop.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want a crooked three-storey bookshop with rotating stock, a restricted shelf and a back room so that visiting Mirela is a highlight.
src/content/bookshops/lamplit-stacks.json from the e21 template: regional pool (licensed schools), rotating shelf, rare conditional stock (e.g. restored after dungeon finds), buyback counter, The Vesperine Hours (sale or loan). Interior: three floors, red shelf, reading nook, Mortimer's rare shelf, the curtain and back-room door (content behind them is e24-stacks-back-room).

## Scope
- In: Bookshop data (public stock), interior scene, shelf placements, Vesperine Hours item placement
- Out: Restricted shelf and back room (e24-stacks-back-room)
- Out: Bookshop runtime/UI (E21)
- Out: Mortimer behaviour (e14-mortimer)
- Out: Spellbook flavour text (e39-spellbook-flavor)

## Notes
Follow the bible's legality: Illusion/Conjuration/Gravity/Shadow restricted; Necromancy/Time/Somnomancy forbidden.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given lamplit-stacks.json, when pnpm validate:bookshops runs, then it passes and the 10-rotation simulation shows every pooled book appearing at least once.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the shop at closing hour, when the player is inside, then Mirela asks them to leave and the stock UI closes (edge).
- AC-3 [integration] Given a book sold to the buyback counter, when the stock rotates, then it may appear in public stock per the e21 rules.
- AC-4 [content] Given the shop, when validated, then The Vesperine Hours is obtainable by purchase or loan on day 1.

items.title: Author the Stacks' restricted shelf and forbidden back room
items.description:
## Why
Some books are expensive, forbidden, hidden or stolen; Mirela's curtain and back room are where the sorcerer's best finds live.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want a restricted shelf that opens when Mirela trusts me and a back room holding a book she will never sell so that trust and theft both matter.
Restricted shelf (Mirror Self, Gravity Well and other restricted schools — writ or Trusted disposition), back room with Nine Sleeps on a locked lectern (never for sale; readable; stealable, teaching Lull), Court-seal markings, and Mirela's reaction facts.

## Scope
- In: Secret/restricted stock data, back-room scene dressing, Nine Sleeps placement, reaction facts
- Out: Public stock (e24-lamplit-stacks)
- Out: Forbidden-book side effects (e07-forbidden-books)

## Notes
Legality per story bible §3.3. Rumour 7 resolves on first restricted-shelf reveal.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given disposition below Trusted and no writ, when viewing the restricted shelf, then its stock is hidden; at Trusted it appears and rumour 7 resolves.
- AC-2 [integration] Given Nine Sleeps, when the player attempts to buy it, then it is not for sale; when stolen, then theft is recorded and Mirela reacts on the next visit (edge).
- AC-3 [content] Given the secret stock data, when pnpm validate:bookshops runs, then every restricted book carries the restricted legality tag and no forbidden book is purchasable.

items.title: Build the Forge, Fletchery & Simples and Bakery with merchant stock
items.description:
## Why
Merchants have identities, inventories and specialties; each shop should serve a class fantasy.

## What
As a player, I want Oswin's forge, Juniper's fletchery and Hollis's bakery to feel like places with people so that shopping is part of the world.
Interiors and merchant data: Brand's Forge (weapons, armour repair service, lockpicks "for miners", Ember-heats-forge discount, bell mould for recasting the tongue), Fenn's Fletchery & Simples (arrows, trick-arrow schematics, snares, salves, wakeful tea vs sleep-draught), Pell's Bakery (bread — also feed for the sleepers, Pell family Bible in the back room).

## Scope
- In: Three interiors, three merchant files, services, key story items placement
- Out: Dialogue (e39-dialogue-town-secondary)
- Out: Economy balancing (e20-economy-balance-tool)

## Notes
Juniper sells poisons to thieves only after a favour (condition on fact).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the three merchant files, when validated, then they pass e20 schema checks and price bands.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the sorcerer casts any heat stimulus on the forge hearth, when Oswin is next spoken to, then a discount effect applies once.
- AC-3 [integration] Given Juniper's stock, when the player has no favour fact, then poisons are hidden (edge); with it, they appear.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the tongue is lost or destroyed, when asked, then Oswin offers the recast service using the bell mould.

items.title: Build the Watch House and a jail cell whose drain leads out
items.description:
## Why
"Caught stealing in town — Hale jails you. The cell has a loose stone." Jail is a secret entrance, not a game over.

## What
As a thief, I want getting caught to put me in a cell with a way out so that failure opens a new route.
Watch House interior (Hale's desk with the missing-persons list and footprint map, boots by the door), one cell. Jail outcome of e22-crime-bounty places the player at this cell's jail spawn and confiscates stolen goods into this settlement's evidence chest. Loose stone (interactable, or found by searching) → Vesperine drain → cistern node.

## Scope
- In: Interior, cell with jail spawn, settlement evidence container, drain passage to cistern
- Out: Crime, bounty and jail outcome logic (e22-crime-bounty)
- Out: Guard arrest AI (E11)
- Out: Cistern (e24-glen-well-cistern)

## Notes
Snig can be jailed here too; busting him out uses the same drain.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the e22-crime-bounty jail outcome for Briar Glen, when applied, then the player stands in this cell and stolen items are in the Watch House evidence chest.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the player in the cell, when the loose stone is interacted with, then the drain opens and leads to the cistern node.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player escapes, when Hale next sees them, then fact jail.escaped is set and his greeting changes (edge: no instant re-arrest loop).

items.title: Build Vane House as an infiltration target with strongbox and ledger
items.description:
## Why
The thief can have proof of Vane's lie before Act II; the house is the town's infiltration set piece.

## What
As a thief, I want to break into the mine owner's house by rooftop or cellar so that I can steal the horn-coin sample and his secrets.
Two-storey house on the rise: servants and a house guard on schedules, study with the strongbox (horn-coin samples, letter from "Mr. S—"), Vane's mine key (for the mine gate), dogs-free garden with hedges, balcony window, coal-chute cellar. Day: Vane receives visitors; night: guard patrol.

## Scope
- In: Interior and grounds, patrols, strongbox and contents, mine key placement, three entry points
- Out: Vane dialogue (e39-dialogue-town-secondary)
- Out: Strongbox lock mechanics (e10-lockpicking)

## Notes
Entry points: balcony window (climb/levitate/rope arrow), coal chute (thief/any), front door (persuade, or bribe the servant).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given night patrols, when the stealth scenario replay enters via the balcony, then the strongbox can be opened with no guard reaching Alerted.
- AC-2 [content] Given the house, when validated, then at least three entry points are declared as obstacle routes for >= 3 classes.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player is detected, when the guard raises the alarm, then a crime is reported via e22-crime-bounty and the jail outcome remains available (edge: failure lands in jail).
- AC-4 [integration] Given the mine key is taken, when the mine gate is approached, then the key opens the padlock via the keyring.

items.title: Hide the cistern route under the Glen Well
items.description:
## Why
"Wells can conceal tunnels." The rumour "drop a stone and you hear it land twice" should pay off.

## What
As a curious player, I want to find a loose ladder rung in the Glen Well that leads to an old cistern so that the town connects to the priory.
Well shaft with a loose rung (climb down, or drop down and take fall damage), echo behaviour (a dropped object produces two landing sounds via a ledge), flooded cistern chambers (wade, freeze to cross, or swim), Snig's goblin tunnels branch, jail drain junction, and a gate to the priory end (E26).

## Scope
- In: Well and cistern scene, echo ledge, water volumes, junctions to jail drain, goblin tunnels and priory
- Out: Priory side of the cistern (e26-priory-greybox)

## Notes
Sets fact well.tunnel.found (resolves rumour 4).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given any object dropped into the well, when it lands, then two landing noise events fire about 0.4 s apart.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the player reaches the cistern, when entered, then well.tunnel.found is set and rumour 4 resolves.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player drops down the shaft instead of climbing, when landing, then fall damage applies but never kills from full health (edge).
- AC-4 [integration] Given the flooded chamber, when frozen by any cold stimulus, then it becomes walkable ice.

items.title: Build the lychgate cemetery and the empty schoolhouse
items.description:
## Why
Quiet places carry the story: Vesperine graves and a teacher's empty desk.

## What
As a player, I want to find lore in the cemetery and schoolhouse so that the town's history and its missing people feel real.
Cemetery: lychgate, Vesperine graves with epitaphs (Hornfolk ear-covering motif on the oldest), Mooring family plot, a fresh unmarked grave (false alarm, humour beat). Schoolhouse: Mina Coles' desk, the skipping rhyme on the slate, Tansy's reading corner, a torn page from The Ox Beneath the Hill.

## Scope
- In: Two small scenes/areas, readable epitaphs and slate, lore item placements
- Out: Text content (e39-books-lore)

## Notes
The torn last page links to Tansy's copy of the book (lore payoff).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given both areas, when validated, then every readable references an existing text id.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the player reads the slate rhyme, when complete, then fact lore.rhyme.read is set (used by Mirela dialogue).
- AC-3 [integration] Given night, when the player enters the cemetery, then no hostile creature spawns there (tone rule: the lights are on in town, edge).

items.title: Build a rooftop network across Briar Glen for thieves and climbers
items.description:
## Why
Town infiltration and verticality: the thief should be able to cross town without touching the street.

## What
As a thief, I want climbable drainpipes, ivy and connected roofs so that I can move above the watch.
Roof paths linking the Ox, the Stacks (third-floor window), the Forge chimney, the Watch House, and the rise to Vane House. Gaps jumpable, some requiring a plank (movable) or rope arrow. Archer overlooks; sorcerer Levitate/Blink shortcuts.

## Scope
- In: Climbable surfaces, roof walk surfaces with acoustic tags, window entries, gap props
- Out: Climbing mechanics (e10-climbing, e02-climb-surfaces)

## Notes
Roof tiles are noisy (acoustic tag loose-tile) in places — a deliberate risk.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the rooftop replay, when a thief crosses from the Ox to Vane House, then they never touch street navmesh.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a loose-tile roof section, when walked at run speed, then footstep noise loudness exceeds that of slates by >= 50%.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a player falls from a roof, when landing on the street, then fall damage is applied and the watch reacts only if in sight (edge).

items.title: Place Briar Glen's NPCs on day/night schedules
items.description:
## Why
A lived-in town: people open shops, go to the inn, sleep — and some walk in their sleep.

## What
As a player, I want townsfolk to keep daily routines so that the town feels alive and so that timing matters for thieves.
Schedule data (consumer of e27-world-clock, which leaves NPC routines to consumers) per named NPC (Mirela, Hale, Vane, Dot, Hollis, Juniper, Oswin, Duggan pre-capture) and 8–12 generic townsfolk: windows (time range → location/activity) built on e11-patrol-routines posts and the world clock. Shop hours bound to merchant hours. Hale sleepwalks toward the Bell Line stones on unlocked nights (Captain's Boots).

## Scope
- In: Schedule schema (thin layer on patrol routines + clock windows), schedule data for all town NPCs, shop hours
- Out: Off-screen catch-up engine (Related: e27-offscreen-catchup, P2 — not needed: positions are resolved directly from the schedule at load)
- Out: Dialogue (E39)

## Notes
The clock and scheduler are e27-world-clock; this item adds only the thin schedule-window schema and all Briar Glen routine data.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given Mirela's schedule and time 08:00, when resolved, then her target is the Stacks counter; at 22:00, her upstairs room.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the player enters town at 14:00 after being away, when loaded, then every NPC is placed at their scheduled location for 14:00.
- AC-3 [integration] Given an NPC is in dialogue when their window ends, when the dialogue closes, then they walk to the next location (edge: never teleport in view).
- AC-4 [perf] Given all scheduled NPCs present at Market Green midday, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).

items.title: Stage the first-night sleepwalk from the Ox to the mine gate
items.description:
## Why
The first night is the tutorial and the hook: follow Tansy, fail gracefully, see the horned shadow.

## What
As a player, I want to follow a sleepwalking child through the silent town so that I learn to move, sneak and interact while the mystery lands.
Night 1 is held: a rest veto (e27-rest-points veto registry) blocks resting until the beat resolves. Tansy's path: bakery → Market Green → mine road → Briarwood edge → mine gate. She cannot be woken (shaking raises her hum). Wolves let her pass. Tutorial prompts along the path. The beat always ends with the horned shape lifting her at the gate — even if the player falls behind (fallback trigger), gets lost, or is blocked.

## Scope
- In: Tansy sleepwalk path, rest veto while night 1 is active, tutorial prompt markers, gate cinematic trigger, fallback triggers
- Out: Text (e39-intro-endings-text)
- Out: Quest graph (e39-main-quest-data)

## Notes
Spans town and Briarwood edge; the gate exterior itself is e25-mine-gate-approach.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the player follows Tansy, when she reaches the gate, then the horned-shape beat plays and fact night1.shadowSeen is set.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the player loses Tansy for 60 s, when the fallback fires, then the beat still resolves with the shadow seen from the nearest vantage (edge).
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player shakes Tansy, when interacted, then her hum loudness rises and she does not wake.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given a new game, when the first-night replay runs, then morning begins at the Ox with night1.shadowSeen set.

items.title: Place the rumour set on sources and wire targets to real facts
items.description:
## Why
"NPC rumors can lead somewhere." Each of the twelve rumours must point at something placed.

## What
As a player, I want rumours from Dot, townsfolk and goblins to lead to real places so that talking becomes exploring.
Bind e39 rumour data to sources (Dot, townsfolk tags, goblins) and ensure each rumour's resolvesWhen fact is produced by placed content (well echo, Mooring armour, stamped trinkets, cracked bell, ledger, restricted shelf, Hale's boots, millpond lantern, the Fold, Clatter, the Standing Horn).

## Scope
- In: Source bindings, fact producers placed where missing, validation run
- Out: Rumour text (e39-rumor-set)
- Out: Rumour runtime (e22-rumors)

## Notes
Rumours 10–11 come from goblins (E26 camp).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the rumour set, when validated, then all 12 rumours have >= 1 source and a produced resolvesWhen fact (no warnings).
- AC-2 [integration] Given rumour 4 heard and the cistern entered, when evaluated, then it resolves as Investigated.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the false rumour 3 (goblins took them), when the Framed in Brass proof is found, then it resolves with a "false" journal note (edge).

items.title: Place Briar Glen's secrets, lore books and hidden treasure
items.description:
## Why
Interesting-looking places should usually contain something interesting; every bookshelf has a book.

## What
As a curious player, I want secrets in town — stashes, notes, books — so that exploring town pays off.
Placement: every bookshelf gets a book, Dot's stamped trinket in the cellar, Hale's dusty boots (Captain's Boots clue), the Pell family Bible, the "friend below" note under the player's door, a thief stash on the Forge roof, a chimney cache, and 6–10 small treasures per the e18 treasure guide.

## Scope
- In: Lore/treasure placements, discovery rules, fact ids
- Out: Text (e39-books-lore)
- Out: Loot tables design (e18-treasure-design-guide)

## Notes
Density target from e18-treasure-design-guide.

- AC-2 [integration] Given the player morning 1, when they leave the room, then the "friend below" note is at the door and readable.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a hidden stash taken, when saved and reloaded, then it stays empty (edge).

items.title: Author class routes for Briar Glen's obstacles
items.description:
## Why
Town obstacles (Vane House, restricted shelf, jail, Watch House records) should open differently per class.

## What
As a player of any class, I want my class to open town obstacles its own way so that town reflects my fantasy.
First-pass routes from the route matrix: knight (persuade via rank, force the coal-chute grate), archer (rope arrow to balcony, shoot the gate latch), sorcerer (Mage Hand the study key, Levitate to window, trade favours with Mirela), thief (lockpick, rooftops, pickpocket keys). Declared in the obstacle registry.

## Scope
- In: Route affordances in town scenes, registry entries, replays for each route
- Out: Gap closing after audit (e16-gap-pass-surface)

## Notes
Uses the route matrix ids verbatim.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the registry, when validated, then every E24 obstacle has >= 3 class routes declared.
- AC-2 [integration] Given each declared route, when replayed, then the obstacle exit fact is set.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a route that relies on an NPC schedule window, when attempted outside the window, then an alternative route for that class still exists (edge).

items.title: Art-dress Briar Glen with final environment assets
items.description:
## Why
The lights are on in town: warmth and hedgerow charm must read at a glance.

## What
As a player, I want Briar Glen to look like a crooked, bookish mining town so that it feels like a place worth saving.
Replace grey-box with approved modular town kit, props and textures; keep collision, navmesh and gameplay entity ids unchanged.

## Scope
- In: Swap grey-box to final meshes/materials, prop dressing, signage, decals
- Out: Asset creation (E37 prompt/generate/integrate beads)

Related: final assets come from E37/E38 per-asset prompt/generate/integrate beads created by the asset-prompt wave from plan/world-asset-needs.md; those integrate beads should block this item. Gameplay never waits on this item.

- AC-1 [integration] Given the dressed town, when the e2e town tour and all town route replays run, then they pass unchanged.
- AC-2 [perf] Given the dressed town at Market Green, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent) and draw calls <= 1500.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the art review, when compared to the style bible, then no building uses colours outside the palette (edge: consistency).

items.title: Light and score Briar Glen for day, dusk and night
items.description:
## Why
Every warm room has one thing that makes you uneasy; lighting and ambience carry that.

## What
As a player, I want town days to sound busy and nights to go quiet so that the sleepwalking dread lands.
Lighting presets per phase, lit windows by schedule, lamplighter relighting; ambience beds (market day, night crickets, forge hammering near the forge, inn murmur); music cues for town day/night/first night; reverb zones for interiors.

## Scope
- In: Lighting setup, ambience zones, music cue bindings, reverb zones
- Out: Audio assets (E38)
- Out: Adaptive music engine (e28-adaptive-music)

## Notes
Related: final assets come from E37/E38 per-asset prompt/generate/integrate beads created by the asset-prompt wave from plan/world-asset-needs.md; those integrate beads should block this item. Gameplay never waits on this item. Related: e28-ambience, e28-reverb-zones and e29-environment-fx are P2 in the combat plan; bind ambience beds, reverb zones and fog/firefly FX here when they land, otherwise ship lighting + music only.

- AC-2 [integration] Given night, when sampling light at Market Green away from lamps, then the level is dark enough for thief visibility < 0.3 while crouched (edge: stealth must remain viable).
- AC-3 [perf] Given night with all lamps lit, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).

items.title: Perf-pass and playtest Briar Glen on both presets
items.description:
## Why
The town is the densest scene (NPCs, lights, props); it is the likeliest perf failure.

## What
Run the perf suite on the town (day/night, full schedules, a street fire) on reference and low-tier machines; run a 5-tester town playtest (can they find the Stacks, the well, Vane House entries unprompted?). Record in docs/playtests/briar-glen.md; file beads.

## Scope
- In: Perf captures, fixes within budget, playtest session and findings
- Out: Global perf work (E32)

## Notes
Related: e32-reference-runbook.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [perf] Given Market Green at midday with full schedules, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).
- AC-2 [perf] Given the same scene on the Low preset, when measured, then p95 <= 16.7 ms at 1080p on the Low preset on an Intel Iris Xe / base M1 8 GB class machine, with p99 <= 33.3 ms (30 fps floor) during worst-case combat.
- AC-3 [perf] Given a warm cache, when entering town from the Briarwood, then the transition completes in <= 3 s and heap stays <= 1.5 GB.
- AC-4 [manual] Given 5 testers, when asked to find the bookshop, the well and a way into Vane House, then >= 4 find all three without help within 20 minutes.

items.title: Block out the Briarwood with paths, clearings and the priory road
items.description:
## Why
The wilderness ties town, tower, mine and priory together; its paths must loop.

## What
As a player, I want a thick old forest with readable paths and hidden side trails so that exploring it feels dense but navigable.
Grey-box Briarwood (~300×250 m): town edge, main trail, Sleepers' Path corridor, Standing Horn clearing, wolf den hollow, woodcutter's hut, millpond and drowned lane, priory road up the hill, spur trail to Mooring's Watch, mine road junction. Terrain with bramble walls (flammable, cuttable) forming soft boundaries. (The Briarwood → Sleeping Ox wake rule is authored in e24-sleeping-ox.)

## Scope
- In: Terrain blockout, path network, bramble boundaries, connectivity nodes, region volume used by respawn rules
- Out: Per-location content (other E25 items)
- Out: Foliage art (e25-wilds-art-dress)

## Notes
Bramble walls are systemic: burning them opens shortcuts (with fire-spread risk, Juniper's fear).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the scene, when validated, then every bible Briarwood location has a named node linked in connectivity.json.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a bramble wall, when it burns, then the navmesh link behind it opens and fire spread is capped at a 12 m radius (edge: no forest-wide fire).
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player stands anywhere in the Briarwood, when the region is queried, then it reports region briarwood (used by respawn rules).
- AC-4 [perf] Given the grey-box forest with placeholder trees, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).

items.title: Reveal the Sleepers' Path at night or to a tracker's eye
items.description:
## Why
The trail of trampled ferns is the forest's mystery and the archer's signature clue.

## What
As an archer, I want to see the Sleepers' Path when others cannot so that my tracking fantasy pays off.
A fern-trail decal set visible when time.phase is night (any class, low contrast) or always to players with sense.tracking (archer), or with Arcane Sight / a lantern held low. Leads from town to the mine gate with a branch to the priory (sets path.found; unlocks Captain's Boots shortcut knowledge).

## Scope
- In: Trail decal entities with visibility conditions, branch to priory, fact wiring
- Out: Tracking capability definition (e19-archer-arrow-channel / class data)

## Notes
If sense.tracking does not exist in class data, raise a bead with systems; fallback is night-only visibility.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given day and a non-archer, when looking at the trail, then it is not rendered; at night it is rendered at low contrast.
- AC-2 [integration] Given an archer with sense.tracking at noon, when looking at the trail, then it is rendered at full contrast.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player follows the branch to the priory, when reached, then path.found is set and the priory shortcut is known on the map (edge: sets once).

items.title: Place the Standing Horn menhir and its readable inscription
items.description:
## Why
Statues speak through posture; the menhir teaches the Hornfolk visual language early.

## What
As a player, I want a Hornfolk stone with hands over its ears so that I start to understand the people who built the Knot.
Clearing with the menhir (hands over ears), an inscription band readable in part by any class and fully by a sorcerer holding Hornfolk fragments (reveals the first rule of the Knot), a hidden horn-coin under a root, and a quiet spot where the song is audible at night (hint of what is below).

## Scope
- In: Menhir placement, inscription readable with conditions, hidden coin, night audio emitter
- Out: Inscription text (e39-books-lore)

## Notes
Resolves rumour 12.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a sorcerer with the Hornfolk fragment item, when reading, then the full inscription shows and lore.knot.rule1 is set.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a non-sorcerer, when reading, then a partial translation shows and no fact is set (edge).
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player reaches the clearing, when entered, then rumour 12 resolves.

items.title: Build the wolf den encounter with feed, scare, sneak and fight routes
items.description:
## Why
The silent pack is the first creature encounter with real options.

## What
As a player, I want to deal with the Briar Wolf pack my own way so that my first wilderness threat has choices.
Den hollow with 4–5 wolves, carcass bait spot, rocky overlooks (archer), bramble cover (thief), a fallen log bridge (knight shoves to block a flank), fire pit (scare). Juniper's hunting snare cache nearby. Pack-memory facts drive later reactions.

## Scope
- In: Encounter placement, overlooks, cover, bait spot, snare cache
- Out: Wolf behaviour (e13-briar-wolves)

## Notes
Resolves rumour 1 when observing wolves ignoring a sleepwalker (first night or later).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the player drops meat at the bait spot, when the pack eats, then the den path can be crossed without combat for 120 s.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a thief crouched in bramble cover at night, when crossing, then no wolf exceeds Suspicious in the scenario replay.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the pack is killed, when the player returns in the "Vespers Rung" ending, then the den is empty rather than respawned (edge: pack memory).

items.title: Build the millpond and drowned lane with a Hushling and a lost lantern
items.description:
## Why
"Something at the millpond sings on still nights. Not a bird." True, and dangerous.

## What
As a player, I want a flooded lane haunted at night by a voice-mimicking Hushling so that the wilderness foreshadows the Knot.
Millpond with a sluice (open/close changes the lane's water level), the drowned lane (wade, freeze, or drain it), a sleepwalker's lost lantern (item and clue), a single night-only Hushling that mimics one of the missing, and the woodcutter's empty hut nearby (safe rest spot, axe, lore).

## Scope
- In: Pond and lane scene, sluice mechanism, water level states, night-only Hushling spawn, lantern item, woodcutter's hut
- Out: Hushling behaviour (e13-hushlings)

## Notes
Resolves rumour 9. The woodcutter's hut is folded in here as the nearby safe spot.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the sluice is opened, when simulated, then the lane water level drops to wading depth within 20 s.
- AC-2 [integration] Given day, when the lane is entered, then no Hushling is present; at night it spawns and mimics one of the missing by name.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player rings any loud noise source >= 0.85 near it, when propagated, then the Hushling dissipates and does not respawn until the next night (edge).

items.title: Block out Mooring's Watch: courtyard, tower floors, roof and tunnel
items.description:
## Why
The abandoned watchtower is a vertical infiltration space and the gateway to the upper mine.

## What
As a player, I want a ruined tower I can take floor by floor so that it rewards climbing, sneaking or holding ground.
Spur approach, goblin lookout camp below the walls, courtyard, four tower floors (armour stand hall, keeper's quarters with the log, bell cord shaft, roof with the signal mirror), outside climb routes (ivy, broken masonry), and the cellar entrance to the collapsed supply tunnel.

## Scope
- In: Tower blockout, lookout camp area, climb routes, cellar tunnel entry, connectivity
- Out: Encounters (e25-mooring-watch-encounters)
- Out: Mirror puzzle (e25-signal-mirror)

## Notes
Tower volume doubles as the Sentinel leash volume.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the scene, when validated, then the tower volume, roof, bell cord and tunnel entry exist as named entities.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the navmesh, when queried, then the roof is reachable by both the interior stair and at least one exterior climb.
- AC-3 [perf] Given the view from the roof over the valley, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).

items.title: Place the Hollow Sentinels and goblin lookout with class resolutions
items.description:
## Why
The Watch Still Stands: watchword, formal relief, bell cord, dispel, stealth or smash.

## What
As a player of any class, I want to end the watch my class's way so that the tower becomes my safe base.
Sentinels on armour stands named in the keeper's log; goblin lookout (2–3 goblins with an alarm pot) below. Resolutions wired as facts: watchword from the keeper's log (any), knight formal relief, archer shoots the bell cord (watch.ended), sorcerer dispel/overload binding, thief sneaks to the roof, smash. Reward: tower as safe base (rest point), Sergeant Mooring's watch-key, closing line in the log.

## Scope
- In: Creature placement, bell cord shootable, log item, safe-base conversion, rewards
- Out: Quest graph (e39-side-quests-wilds)
- Out: Sentinel behaviour (e13-hollow-sentinels)

## Notes
Resolves rumour 2.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the bell cord hit by any projectile or cut, when it rings, then watch.ended is set and all sentinels stand down.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the watchword read in the log, when spoken to a sentinel, then that sentinel and its peers stand down.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the goblin lookout raises the alarm, when the sentinels hear it, then they do not leave the tower (edge: leash holds).
- AC-4 [integration] Given watch.ended, when the player rests in the keeper's quarters, then it acts as a rest point and respawn location for the region.

items.title: Turn the signal mirror to light the priory's hidden choir door
items.description:
## Why
Redirecting light across a valley is the constitution's puzzle promise at landscape scale.

## What
As a player, I want to rotate the tower's signal mirror at the right time of day so that a beam reveals a hidden door at the priory.
Rotatable mirror prefab on the roof; at day or with a light source/spell at night, the beam aligned to the priory marker sets priory.choirDoor.revealed. Alternatives: Prism Ray from the priory side, the Arcane Sight reveal, or finding the choir door lever from inside.

## Scope
- In: Mirror prefab placement, long-range beam target, cross-scene fact, alternatives declared
- Out: Choir door itself (e26-priory-choir)

## Notes
Beam is simulated in the tower scene and resolves to a fact; no cross-scene physics.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given sun phase day and the mirror rotated to the priory marker, when evaluated, then priory.choirDoor.revealed is set.
- AC-2 [integration] Given night and no light source on the mirror, when rotated to the marker, then nothing happens (edge).
- AC-3 [content] Given the puzzle file, when the solvability validator runs, then >= 2 distinct solutions are found.

items.title: Make the collapsed supply tunnel a class-gated shortcut to the mine
items.description:
## Why
The watchtower-to-mine loop is the "long way in" for any class and a shortcut once cleared.

## What
As a player, I want to clear the collapsed tunnel under the tower so that I reach the upper Deepworks without Vane's gate.
Collapse with routes: knight clears rubble by hand (heavy push/lift), sorcerer Gravity Well or Telekinetic Throw removes key stones, thief squeezes through a gap (crawl), archer shoots a rotten prop to drop a section (then climb), any class with a pick item digs slowly. Clearing sets shortcut.supplyTunnel.

## Scope
- In: Collapse entities, routes, fact wiring to E26 upper mine node
- Out: Mine interior beyond the collapse (e26-deepworks-greybox)

## Notes
Boundary between E25 and E26 is the collapse itself.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the obstacle registry, when validated, then the supply tunnel declares >= 4 class routes.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the collapse cleared by any route, when evaluated, then shortcut.supplyTunnel is set and persists after reload.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the archer drops the rotten prop while standing under it, when it falls, then crush damage applies via environmental damage (edge).

items.title: Build the boarded mine gate with every class's way in
items.description:
## Why
Getting in is the first big class-choice moment (bible §4.1 beat 5).

## What
As a player of any class, I want several ways past Vane's sealed gate so that my class decides how I enter the Deepworks.
Mine gate exterior: Bell Line rule carved above ("No shaft below the Bell Line. The hill is kept."), padlocked gate (Vane's key or lockpick), rotted side-boarding (knight smash), winch pulley (archer shot drops the cage), inner bar (Mage Hand) and rope latch (Ember/any heat), ventilation chimney up the hillside (thief climb). Bell Line boundary stones where Hale's sleepwalk stops.

## Scope
- In: Gate exterior scene, routes, readable carving, Bell Line stones, transition into E26
- Out: Winch house interior (e26-deepworks-greybox)

## Notes
Target 4 classes + the long way (supply tunnel) + the river way (e25-weeping-adit, the sixth entry route, registered as its own obstacle).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the obstacle registry, when validated, then the mine gate declares routes for all four classes plus the key route.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the rope latch exposed to any heat stimulus, when it burns, then the gate unbars.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the knight smashes the side-boarding, when broken, then the gap persists after reload and fact mine.boardsBroken is set (Vane remarks).
- AC-4 [integration] Given the player opens the gate at night while a sleepwalker event is active, when entered, then the sleepwalker path is not blocked (edge).

items.title: Build Briar Glen Quay and the Ore Stair chute down from the mine
items.description:
## Why
The river is the town's second heart; the Ore Stair turns the mine's sorting hall and the quay into a loop.

## What
As a player, I want a working quay below town and a stepped ore chute from the Deepworks so that the river connects to the mine.
Briar Glen Quay: moorings for Mags Oakum's barge Patient Ann, ore bins, bollards, a crane, a toll shed and the barge departure point. The Ore Stair: a stepped chute from the Deepworks ore-sorting hall (goblin camp) down to the quay — slide down one-way from the top (shortcut.oreStair), climbable upward only by climbers or with a rope arrow anchor.

## Scope
- In: Quay scene area, Ore Stair chute with slide and climb routes, connectivity edges to town and the E26 sorting hall
- Out: Barge travel (e25-barge-travel)
- Out: Sorting hall interior (e26-deepworks-greybox)

## Notes
Standing water only: the quay basin is an e03 water volume (wading, swimming, freezing); the river does not flow in the sim.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the player at the top of the Ore Stair in the sorting hall, when they slide down, then they arrive at the quay within 10 s and shortcut.oreStair is set.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a non-climbing player at the quay, when trying to go up the chute, then no route exists until a climb or rope-arrow capability is used (edge).
- AC-3 [integration] Given the quay basin, when any cold stimulus freezes it, then it becomes walkable ice via e03 rules.
- AC-4 [content] Given connectivity.json, when validated, then quay ↔ town and ore-stair (one-way) edges exist with their unlock conditions.

items.title: Build the Millweir and its sluice walk to the Briarwood far bank
items.description:
## Why
The Vesperine-built weir is a river loop: crossing it opens the forest's far bank.

## What
As a player, I want to cross the Millweir on its sluice walk so that I reach the Briarwood's far bank without the long road.
Weir below town with a narrow sluice walk; sluice gates set the standing-water level above and below the weir (two states); the walk is slippery when wet and gains grip when dry; a gap mid-walk needs a plank, a jump, Blink or a rope anchor. Crossing sets shortcut.millweir.

## Scope
- In: Weir scene area, sluice gate mechanism with two water-level states, walk traversal with gap, connectivity edge
- Out: Flowing-water simulation (not planned — water is standing volumes only)

## Notes
Falling off the walk drops the player into the pool below, never kills from full health.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the sluice gate closed, when toggled open, then the upper pool level drops to its low state within 20 s and a submerged stepping stone path is exposed.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the player crosses the walk by any route, when they reach the far bank, then shortcut.millweir is set and persists after reload.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player falls from the walk, when landing in the pool, then they take no fall damage and can swim to the bank (edge).

items.title: Build the Weeping Adit: the flooded sixth way into the lower Deepworks
items.description:
## Why
The river's source is also the mine's back door; going up the Adit is the sixth entry route (bible §4.1 beat 5).

## What
As a player of any class, I want to go up the flooded drainage tunnel where the Wend springs so that I reach the lower Deepworks without Vane's gate.
Adit mouth on the hillside (humming audible at night — rumour 16), a flooded tunnel of standing-water chambers with a push-current volume (external impulse, not a flow sim) at the narrows. Routes: swim with air pockets; freeze the current's edge into an ice ledge (any cold stimulus); ride in on an empty ore barge being winched back up (winch mechanism, timed by Mags' schedule); climb the dry drainage ledge (climbers). Emerges in the Deepworks' flooded lower gallery (E26).

## Scope
- In: Adit mouth and tunnel scene, push-current volume, air pockets, winched-barge ride, ice-ledge route, transition to the E26 flooded gallery
- Out: Lower Deepworks interior (e26-deepworks-greybox)
- Out: Mags' dialogue about the Adit (e39-dialogue-harbor-folk)

## Notes
Registered as its own mine-entry obstacle so the E16 audit counts the Adit separately from the gate. Resolves rumour 16. Buoyancy (e03-buoyancy, P2) is not required: the barge is a mechanism on a winch path.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the push-current volume at the narrows, when a swimming player enters it, then they are pushed back toward the mouth unless they hold to a ledge or the edge is frozen.
- AC-2 [integration] Given any cold stimulus on the current's edge, when frozen, then an ice ledge forms and the narrows can be walked for as long as it stays frozen.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the winch is running and the player rides the empty barge, when it reaches the top, then the player arrives in the flooded lower gallery and mine.entry.adit is set.
- AC-4 [content] Given the obstacle registry, when validated, then the Adit declares >= 3 class routes plus an any-class swim route.
- AC-5 [integration] Given the player runs out of air in the tunnel, when drowning damage would kill them, then they are washed out to the Adit mouth instead (edge: failure moves them, not a reload).

items.title: Build the towpath and Kestrel Lock with the keeper's cottage
items.description:
## Why
The towpath is the always-open road to Wendmouth; Kestrel Lock is its halfway landmark and gossip post.

## What
As a player, I want to walk the towpath down the valley past Kestrel Lock so that I can reach Wendmouth on foot and meet Old Reed.
A compressed towpath route in two legs (Briar Glen Quay → Kestrel Lock → Wendmouth outskirts); each leg transition advances the world clock (6 game hours per leg). Kestrel Lock: two gates and a lock chamber whose standing-water level is raised or lowered by paddles (two states), a lock beam walk, the toll board, and Old Reed's cottage (toll-in-gossip rumour source, rest point).

## Scope
- In: Two towpath legs with transitions and time advance, lock chamber with two water states, paddles, cottage interior, rest point
- Out: Barge travel (e25-barge-travel)
- Out: Old Reed dialogue (e39-dialogue-harbor-folk)
- Out: Toll board text (e39-harbor-rumors-texts)

## Notes
Distances are compressed; the fiction is "a day downriver". Time advance keeps the Tern's Act III departure unaffected (it is quest-gated, not clock-gated).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the player completes a towpath leg transition, when they arrive, then game time has advanced by exactly 6 hours via advanceTime.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the lock paddles are opened, when simulated, then the chamber moves to the other water-level state within 30 s and the lower gate can be opened only when levels match.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player tries to open a lock gate against unequal levels, when interacted, then it refuses with a visible strain cue and no state change (edge).
- AC-4 [perf] Given the lock with the cottage and towpath foliage in view, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).

items.title: Ride Mags Oakum's barge between Briar Glen Quay and Wendmouth
items.description:
## Why
Wendmouth must be quick to reach from the morning after the first night; a narrated barge ride is the fast way.

## What
As a player, I want to pay Mags for passage on the Patient Ann so that I travel downriver in one narrated ride instead of walking.
Travel service at Briar Glen Quay, Kestrel Lock and the Wendmouth Ore Wharf: departs mornings only (refuses at night: "not with whatever's singing up there"); downriver advances 1 game day, upriver 2 (towed); a short narrated ride card with class-flavoured Mags lines; optional stowaway under the tarpaulin (thief, for a fee) that skips the customs inspection on arrival. Available from the morning after night 1.

## Scope
- In: Travel service data and runtime (fare, schedule window, direction durations), ride card UI hook, stowaway flag, arrival spawn points
- Out: Flowing-water or boat-handling simulation (not planned)
- Out: Ride text (e39-dialogue-harbor-folk)
- Out: Customs inspection (e40-customs-house)

## Notes
No other plan owns fast travel; this is deliberately a narrow travel-service item, reusable later for other routes.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given the player at the quay at 08:00 on day 2 with the fare, when they board downriver, then they arrive at the Wendmouth Ore Wharf at 08:00 on day 3 and the fare is deducted.
- AC-2 [unit] Given an upriver trip, when taken, then exactly 2 game days elapse and time events fire in order via advanceTime.
- AC-3 [integration] Given night or night 1 not yet resolved, when the player asks for passage, then Mags refuses and no time passes (edge).
- AC-4 [integration] Given the stowaway option taken, when arriving at Wendmouth, then the customs inspection trigger is skipped for that arrival only.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given a save at the quay, when the player rides down and back, then both arrivals load in <= 3 s warm with zero console errors.

items.title: Art-dress, light and score the River Wend locations
items.description:
## Why
The river should read as the valley's working artery: tarred wood, brown water, herons and barges.

## What
As a player, I want the quay, Millweir, Adit, towpath and Kestrel Lock to look and sound like the story bible so that the river has identity.
Final environment kit and props for the river locations, water surface materials for standing-water volumes, lighting per time-of-day, the river music cue and river ambience bindings; gameplay ids and collision unchanged.

## Scope
- In: Art swap for five river locations, water material presets, lighting, music/ambience bindings
- Out: Asset creation (E37/E38)

## Notes
Related: final assets come from E37/E38 per-asset prompt/generate/integrate beads created by the asset-prompt wave from plan/world-asset-needs.md; those integrate beads should block this item. - AC-2 [integration] Given the player enters any river location, when crossing its trigger, then the river music cue plays within 3 s.
- AC-3 [perf] Given the quay with the barge, crane and water surface in view, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent) and p95 <= 16.7 ms at 1080p on the Low preset on an Intel Iris Xe / base M1 8 GB class machine, with p99 <= 33.3 ms (30 fps floor) during worst-case combat (edge: water shader on Low).

items.title: Author class routes and ability-gated shortcuts across the wilderness
items.description:
## Why
Paths loop together and reveal shortcuts as players acquire abilities.

## What
As a player of any class, I want new abilities to open new wilderness shortcuts so that returning to the forest feels different.
Shortcuts: rope-arrow anchor up the priory crag, the Millweir gap (plank/jump/Blink/rope), climbing the Ore Stair upward, frozen millpond crossing, bramble burn-through to the tower spur, a climbable ravine to the mine hillside, a Blink gap over the drowned lane. Registry entries and replays.

## Scope
- In: Shortcut affordances, registry entries, replays, connectivity updates
- Out: Gap closing after audit (e16-gap-pass-surface)

## Notes
Each shortcut is one-way until opened from the far side where sensible.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the registry, when validated, then every E25 obstacle has >= 3 class routes.
- AC-2 [integration] Given each shortcut, when opened, then its fact persists and connectivity reachability updates.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a frozen-pond crossing, when the ice melts while the player is on it, then the player drops into water and can swim out (edge).

items.title: Place wilderness and river secrets, lore caches and treasure
items.description:
## Why
The world rewards curiosity: a hollow tree, a drowned cart, a goblin stash.

## What
As a curious player, I want hidden things in the Briarwood and the tower so that detours pay.
Placement: Tansy's hair ribbon on the mine rail, the keeper's log pages, a goblin stash in a hollow oak, a drowned cart in the lane, a Juniper snare cache, a spellbook page in the woodcutter's hut, Mags' split-plank horn-coin at the quay, the Kestrel Lock toll board, a lost cargo crate in the lock chamber, and 8–12 small treasures.

## Scope
- In: Placements, discovery rules, facts
- Out: Text (e39-books-lore, e39-item-creature-text)

## Notes
Use e18 treasure density guidance.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the wilderness scenes, when audited, then every "interesting-looking" landmark tag has >= 1 placed discovery.
- AC-2 [integration] Given Tansy's ribbon picked up, when inspected, then its item text matches e39 text ids.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a cache looted, when saved and reloaded, then it remains empty (edge).

items.title: Art-dress the Briarwood and Mooring's Watch with final assets
items.description:
## Why
The forest must feel old and thick — oak, holly, bramble — without hurting perf.

## What
As a player, I want the Briarwood and the watchtower to look like the story bible describes so that the region has identity.
Foliage (instanced), terrain textures, ruined tower kit, props; keep collision and gameplay ids intact.

## Scope

items.title: Light and score the wilderness for day, night and still nights
items.description:
## Why
The wolves' silence and the song on still nights are sound-design beats.

## What
As a player, I want the forest to sound alive by day and wrong by night so that dread builds before the dungeon.
Lighting per phase with moonlight and fog; ambience beds (forest day, forest night without wolf howls, millpond water, tower wind); music cues for Briarwood explore and Mooring's Watch; fireflies and fog volumes.

## Scope
- In: Lighting, ambience zones, music bindings, environment FX placement
- Out: Audio assets (E38)

## Notes
Related: final assets come from E37/E38 per-asset prompt/generate/integrate beads created by the asset-prompt wave from plan/world-asset-needs.md; those integrate beads should block this item. Gameplay never waits on this item. Related: e28-ambience, e28-reverb-zones and e29-environment-fx are P2 in the combat plan; bind ambience beds, reverb zones and fog/firefly FX here when they land, otherwise ship lighting + music only.
items.acceptance:

- AC-2 [integration] Given the player enters Mooring's Watch, when crossing the trigger, then the music crossfades to the tower cue within 3 s.

items.title: Perf-pass and playtest the wilderness on both presets
items.description:
## Why
Foliage-heavy scenes are the classic browser perf trap.

## What
Perf suite runs over Briarwood, Mooring's Watch, the quay, the Adit and Kestrel Lock on reference and low-tier machines; a 5-tester navigation playtest (can they find the tower, the den and the mine gate without a map?). Findings and beads in docs/playtests/wilderness.md.

## Scope

## Notes
Related: e32-reference-runbook.
items.acceptance:
