items.title: Design the dungeon network: areas, routes, puzzles and endings
items.description:
## Why
"One fantastic dungeon with interconnected systems beats ten generic dungeons" — it needs a master plan.

## What
docs/design/dungeon.md: area graph for the Deepworks, Bellwater Priory and the Knot; critical path vs optional; macro-routes per class; placement of the six MVP puzzles (Sunbeam, Frozen Channel, Scales, Watchers, Dark Crossing, Chimes); shortcut list; encounter pacing chart; Fold respawn logic; set pieces (sour bell, Horn's Hall, Cradle, climb, Vespers); level-state table for the four endings.

## Scope
- In: Design doc, area graph additions to connectivity.json, puzzle placement table, ending state table
- Out: Puzzle mechanics (E15)
- Out: Quest graph (e39-main-quest-data)

## Notes
Puzzle placement: Frozen Channel in the Deepworks flooded gallery; Sunbeam in the priory crypt stair; Watchers = choir statues; Scales at the Outer Ring Hornfolk gate; Dark Crossing in the Ossuary pit; Chimes in the Chapel of Echoes.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the doc, when reviewed, then each of the six puzzles is placed in a named area with its reference puzzle key (e15-reference-puzzles-a/b).
- AC-2 [content] Given the area graph, when validated with connectivity.json, then every area is reachable and the Cradle is reachable by >= 2 macro-routes.
- AC-3 [content] Given the ending table, when reviewed, then each of the four endings lists the world facts and the level variants it changes.
- AC-4 [content] Given the pacing chart, when reviewed, then no two combat-heavy areas are adjacent on the critical path without a quiet area between (edge: pacing).

items.title: Block out the Deepworks: winch house, galleries, goblin hall, breach
items.description:
## Why
The mine is the dungeon's first layer and the goblins' home.

## What
As a player, I want an abandoned silver mine with levels, rails and a cage lift so that descending feels like a journey.
Winch house and cage lift, upper galleries with mine-cart rails, the old ore-sorting hall (goblin camp), the supply-tunnel arrival point, the flooded lower gallery (Frozen Channel site and the arrival point of the Weeping Adit river route), the Ore Stair chute head in the sorting hall, Vane's sealed lower gallery below the Bell Line, and the breach into the Knot's Outer Ring.

## Scope
- In: Mine scene blockout, cage lift mechanism, rails, connectivity nodes, breach transition
- Out: Encounters (e26-deepworks-encounters)
- Out: Gallery/breach content (e26-vane-gallery-breach)

## Notes
Mine decision: the Deepworks interior is E26; exterior gate and supply tunnel collapse are E25.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the scene, when validated, then every bible Deepworks location exists as a named node, including the Adit arrival and the Ore Stair head.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the cage lift, when its winch is operated or its pulley shot, then it descends and the lower level becomes reachable.
- AC-3 [perf] Given the ore-sorting hall grey-box, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).

items.title: Populate the Deepworks: goblin camp, miner Forgotten, mine hazards
items.description:
## Why
The goblin camp can be fought, sneaked through or talked to — the space must support all three.

## What
As a player, I want a goblin camp with lookouts, alarms and side passages so that I choose between talking, sneaking and fighting.
Camp layout (Kettleback's kettle throne, Duggan's crate, hammocks incl. Snig's with the primer, alarm pots), patrols, lookouts; miner Forgotten hauling ore below; systemic objects: oil lamps, mine carts (pushable, ride-able downhill), rotten supports (breakable collapse), spilled lamp-oil channels (flammable liquid), the sleepwalker scrawl "it's so pretty down here".

## Scope
- In: Creature placement and patrols, props with material presets, alarm devices, side passages
- Out: Social behaviour (E14)
- Out: Goblin combat (e13-rootcellar-goblins)

## Notes
Goblin rumours 10–11 are sourced here. Related: e03-gas-clouds (P2) — if it lands, add a firedamp pocket that explodes on ignition.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a thief entering via the side vent at night, when the stealth replay runs, then Duggan's crate is reachable without any goblin reaching Alerted.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a spilled lamp-oil channel under a rotten support, when any heat source ignites the oil, then the fire spreads along the channel and the burnt support collapses.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a mine cart pushed downhill into goblins, when it hits, then knockback applies via physics impulse (not scripted).
- AC-4 [integration] Given every alarm pot is destroyed beforehand, when the camp is alerted, then goblins fall back to shouting (edge: alarm degraded, not broken).

items.title: Build Vane's sealed gallery, the ledger and the sealable breach
items.description:
## Why
The gallery holds the proof of Vane's lie; sealing the breach is the best outcome's key act.

## What
As a player, I want to find Vane's ledger and the horn-ring and seal the breach so that I can expose him and restore the Knot's sentence.
Sealed gallery door (Vane key, pick, smash), gallery 9 carvings with pry marks, the Deepworks Ledger, the horn-ring pried from a carving, the breach. Sealing options (fact breach.sealed): collapse Vane's tunnel (break supports / Thunderclap), freeze and shore (frozen + timber), or goblins wall it (goblins.hired.breach).

## Scope
- In: Gallery scene content, ledger and horn-ring items, three sealing routes
- Out: Framed in Brass quest (e39-side-quests-wilds)

## Notes
Sealing should be possible only after horn.befriended (Help path) or explicitly allowed earlier with a warning — decide in e26-dungeon-layout.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the supports broken by any force above threshold, when collapsed, then breach.sealed is set and the breach navmesh link is removed.
- AC-2 [integration] Given goblins.hired.breach, when the player returns, then the wall is built and breach.sealed is set.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player is inside the breach when it collapses, when resolved, then they are pushed to the gallery side, never trapped (edge).

items.title: Block out Bellwater Priory: nave, choir, scriptorium, belfry, crypt
items.description:
## Why
The ruined monastery is the lore heart and the top of the Sounding Shaft.

## What
As a player, I want a roofless priory on the hill with a tall belfry so that climbing it feels like approaching the answer.
Priory road gate, roofless nave, choir with singing-monk statues and the hidden choir door, scriptorium, garden with the dead pear tree, belfry with the cracked Vesper Bell and the top of the Sounding Shaft, crypt (sealed from below), cistern end joining the Glen Well route.

## Scope
- In: Priory blockout, belfry climb, crypt, cistern link, connectivity nodes
- Out: Room content (priory items)

## Notes
Can be visited before Act II via the forest (bible beat 9).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the scene, when validated, then every bible priory location exists as a named node, including the cistern link stub that e24-glen-well-cistern connects to.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the crypt door, when approached from the priory, then it is sealed and has no route from this side until shortcut.crypt is set.
- AC-3 [perf] Given the view from the belfry, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).

items.title: Place the Watchers statue puzzle in the priory choir
items.description:
## Why
Statues that do something; the choir puzzle reveals the pact and the Sounding Shaft.

## What
As a player, I want to turn the singing-monk statues to face the altar so that the choir reveals its secrets.
Watchers puzzle from e15-reference-puzzles-b placed in the choir (rotate, levitate-rotate, or topple one — the destructive solution), rewarding the pact scroll and the abbot's letters cache. The hidden choir door (revealed by the signal mirror, or lever from inside) is a second entry.

## Scope
- In: Puzzle instance, rewards, hidden door states
- Out: Puzzle mechanics (e15-reference-puzzles-b)
- Out: Mirror (e25-signal-mirror)

## Notes
One of the six MVP puzzles.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the placed puzzle, when the solvability validator runs, then >= 2 distinct solutions pass and >= 3 classes can solve it.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a statue is toppled, when evaluated, then the puzzle remains solvable and no softlock is reported (edge).
- AC-3 [integration] Given priory.choirDoor.revealed, when the choir is approached from the garden, then the hidden door is open.

items.title: Build the scriptorium with book mimics, tallow ooze and abbot letters
items.description:
## Why
A library that bites: surviving pages, mimics and wax — and fire is both weapon and risk.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want a ruined scriptorium full of pages, candles and dangers so that curiosity is rewarded and punished.
Book mimics among real shelves; Tallow Ooze in the candle store; the abbot's letters fragments; loose lore and spellbook pages; flammable paper everywhere (fire spreads fast here — burning the room destroys loot).

## Scope
- In: Creature and item placement, flammable density design, page placements
- Out: Mimic and ooze behaviour (E13)
- Out: Letter text (e39-books-lore)

## Notes
Fire destroying lore is a valid, story-creating failure; key lore has a second copy elsewhere. Related: e07-damaged-books (P2) — if it lands, some pages become missing pages of damaged books.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a fire started in the scriptorium, when it burns out, then destroyed pages are recorded as facts and each key lore item has a surviving alternate source.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a book mimic, when the player feeds it a paper item, then it pacifies and yields a page.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the ooze melted by fire, when its puddle ignites, then fire spreads to adjacent flammable shelves (edge: systemic chain).

items.title: Build the belfry and the sour-bell consequence of early ringing
items.description:
## Why
Ringing the bell without its tongue should create a story, not a no-op.

## What
As a player, I want to be able to strike the cracked bell early so that I face the consequence and meet Horn.
Belfry climb, bell frame, bell ropes. Striking the tongueless bell with any heavy impact or loud force (hammer, mace, arrow, Thunderclap) plays a sour note: wakes every Forgotten in the priory, +1 song intensity for 5 minutes, Hushlings rise up the shaft, and Horn comes toward the sound (horn.heardBell).

## Scope
- In: Belfry content, bell impact detection by force/noise, consequence wiring
- Out: The finale ring (e26-vesper-bell-finale)

## Notes
This is a "failure creates stories" beat and a Horn-meeting route.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the tongueless bell struck by any impact >= threshold, when resolved, then a sour-bell event fires and every priory Forgotten enters Searching.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the sour bell, when evaluated, then song.intensity rises by 1 for 300 s and horn.heardBell is set.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the bell struck repeatedly, when evaluated, then consequences apply once per 300 s window (edge: no stacking exploit).

items.title: Block out the Knot's Outer Ring, Ossuary Galleries and Chapel
items.description:
## Why
The labyrinth's outer half is where the Knot's rules are learned.

## What
As a player, I want rune-lined corridors, bone galleries and an echoing chapel so that the labyrinth feels ancient and legible.
Outer Ring (looping corridors with rune bands, spider nests, the Scales gate), Ossuary Galleries (bone niches, Clatter's mushroom garden, the Dark Crossing pit), Chapel of Echoes (acoustic space, portcullis with counterweight, Chimes site). Multiple routes, vents and crawlspaces.

## Scope
- In: Blockout of three areas, loops, vents, portcullis mechanism, connectivity
- Out: Inner Knot (e26-knot-inner-greybox)
- Out: Rune navigation rule (e26-knot-rune-navigation)

## Notes
Budget: each area loads as a separate scene or streamed chunk to keep memory in budget.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the scenes, when validated, then Outer Ring, Ossuary and Chapel exist with >= 2 routes between each adjacent pair.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the Chapel portcullis counterweight hit by any projectile or cut, when it drops, then the portcullis closes.
- AC-3 [perf] Given the Ossuary grey-box, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).

items.title: Block out the Fold, Horn's Hall, Sounding Shaft foot and the Cradle
items.description:
## Why
The inner Knot hosts the reveal, the warden and the climax.

## What
As a player, I want the heart of the labyrinth to feel sacred and strange so that the reveal and finale have a stage.
Horn's Hall (arena outside the Fold), the Fold (sealed vault with moss beds), the crypt passage up to the priory (sealed), the Sounding Shaft foot, the Cradle (round chamber, carved faces turned inward), plus a secret sorcerer route to the Cradle via Hornfolk inscriptions.

## Scope
- In: Blockout of four areas, secret route, connectivity
- Out: Area content (inner Knot items)

## Notes
The Sounding Shaft interior climb is e26-sounding-shaft-climb.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the scenes, when validated, then Horn's Hall, the Fold, the Shaft foot and the Cradle exist and connect per connectivity.json.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the secret route, when the inscription is read by a sorcerer with the fragments, then it opens; otherwise it is a wall (edge).
- AC-3 [perf] Given the Cradle grey-box, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).

items.title: Make the Knot loop unless you follow its runes
items.description:
## Why
The first rule of the Knot — followed runes lead somewhere; ignored runes lead in circles — is the labyrinth's identity.

## What
As a player, I want the labyrinth to quietly loop me back when I ignore the runes so that reading the walls becomes the way through.
Loop junctions: data-driven portal-free loops (corridor segments that reconnect) plus conditional junction doors that route by whether the player followed the rune sequence (tracked per junction). Loom-spider webs copying runes act as clues. Goblins pass freely (cannot read, never caught). Chalk marks from the "friend below" help early.

## Scope
- In: Junction state logic, rune sequence data, web clue placements, chalk mark placements
- Out: Rune text/art (E37/E39)

## Notes
Must never feel like a bug: loops show a recurring landmark (a specific carved face) so players notice.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a junction expecting rune "horn-left" and the player takes the unmarked path, when crossing, then they are routed back to the loop start landmark.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the player follows the rune sequence through 3 junctions, when completed, then they reach the Ossuary entrance.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player loops 3 times at one junction, when evaluated, then a diegetic hint (a web clue lit, a chalk mark) appears (edge: anti-frustration).

items.title: Populate the Outer Ring: spiders, first Forgotten, Horn sighting
items.description:
## Why
Act II's first steps into the Knot must introduce its creatures and the warden at a distance.

## What
As a player, I want my first minutes in the Knot to introduce spiders, the Forgotten and a glimpse of the minotaur so that I feel watched and curious.
Loom spider nests with web routes, the first sweeping Forgotten, a scripted distant sighting of Horn dragging a wrapped figure across a gallery, "friend below" notes and chalk arrows (genuinely helpful), systemic lights (braziers for scaring spiders).

## Scope
- In: Creature placement, sighting trigger, notes and chalk placement, braziers
- Out: Note text (e39-dialogue-abbot)

## Notes
The sighting must not be interactable at range (Horn exits before the player can reach him).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the player crosses the sighting trigger, when fired, then Horn crosses the far gallery and exits within 8 s and fact horn.sighted is set.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a brazier lit near a spider nest, when light exceeds 0.7, then the nest's spiders flee and the web route can be burned.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player shoots at Horn during the sighting, when hit, then he does not engage and still exits (edge).

items.title: Populate the Ossuary: Forgotten habits, Clatter's garden, the psalter
items.description:
## Why
Among the skeletons, one keeps apologising — the Ossuary is where the game's warmest quest begins.

## What
As a player, I want galleries of praying and sweeping dead and one who remembers so that I learn the dead were people.
Monk and miner Forgotten on habit routines, bone piles for scatter/burn tactics, Clatter tending pale mushrooms in the "flower room", his psalter hidden among the niches, the Dark Crossing pit (placed in e26-dungeon-puzzles), holy-water font (consecrated).

## Scope
- In: Creature/habit placement, Clatter spawn, psalter item, font, bone piles
- Out: Clatter logic (e14-clatter)

## Notes
Resolves rumour 11.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a crouched player humming the hymn, when crossing the Ossuary, then no Forgotten enters Combat at song intensity <= 2.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the psalter picked up, when inspected, then clatter.piece.psalter is set.
- AC-3 [integration] Given Clatter killed accidentally while hostile, when evaluated, then he reassembles unless bones burned, and the quest records clatter.harmed (edge).

items.title: Build the Chapel of Echoes with the Chimes puzzle and portcullis trap
items.description:
## Why
Sound misbehaves here: the chapel is the sound puzzle, a Hushling hunting ground and a Horn trap.

## What
As a player, I want a chapel where echoes carry and misdirect so that sound becomes both clue and danger.
Chimes puzzle (e15-reference-puzzles-b) placed: reproduce a chime order heard behind a wall, shoot bells from the balcony, or read the order in a book. Acoustic trick: noise from certain points is re-emitted at mirror points (misdirects hunters). Hushlings patrol. Portcullis trap: lure Horn under it and drop it (horn.trapped) — the archer's single-shot resolution.

## Scope
- In: Puzzle instance, echo emitters, Hushling placement, portcullis trap state
- Out: Echo propagation engine changes (E09) — use noise re-emitters only

## Notes
One of the six MVP puzzles.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the Chimes instance, when validated, then >= 2 solutions pass and >= 3 classes can solve it.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a noise at an echo point, when propagated, then a copy is emitted at the mirror point and Hushlings investigate the mirror point.
- AC-3 [integration] Given Horn pursuing the player under the portcullis, when it drops, then horn.trapped is set and Horn cannot reach the Fold side.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the portcullis dropped with no one under it, when evaluated, then a winch on the far side can raise it (edge: no softlock).

items.title: Place the Frozen Channel, Sunbeam, Scales and Dark Crossing puzzles
items.description:
## Why
The MVP needs ~6 meaningful puzzles built from world systems; four are placed here (Watchers and Chimes in their rooms).

## What
As a player, I want dungeon puzzles that use light, ice, weight and darkness so that the systems I have learned open the way.
Place from e15 references: Frozen Channel (Deepworks flooded gallery), Sunbeam (priory crypt stair, light down to a sensor), Scales (Outer Ring Hornfolk gate — crates, bodies, ice blocks), Dark Crossing (Ossuary pit — torches, light spell, braziers or smoke drafts). Each rethemed to its area with area props.

## Scope
- In: 4 puzzle instances, retheming, solution replays, softlock policies
- Out: Puzzle kit (E15)

## Notes
Zero new TypeScript: engine gaps become E03/E15 beads.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the 4 instances, when the solvability validator runs, then each has >= 2 distinct solutions.
- AC-2 [integration] Given e15-solution-audit, when run, then each is solvable by >= 3 classes at MVP capability levels.
- AC-3 [integration] Given each declared solution, when its replay runs, then the puzzle reaches solved.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the Scales gate solved with an ice block that later melts, when evaluated, then the gate stays open (edge: one-shot).

items.title: Stage Horn's Hall and the Fold, the reveal and the wake-up point
items.description:
## Why
The reveal lands visually before anyone explains it: the missing asleep on moss beds, bread at their sides.

## What
As a player, I want to enter the Fold and see the sleepers safe so that I understand Horn before he says a word.
Horn's Hall arena (pillars, bronze-wired horn racks, Horn's resting spot for the "rests one eye" trick), the Fold door (horn-key on Horn's belt; pickpocketable), the Fold: seven moss beds (six missing + Tansy after night 1), goblin bread, chalk tallies (sleepers and the player's rescues). Respawn rules: death in the Knot wakes here (horn alive); variants: goblin camp (Horn dead, goblins friendly), Forgotten laying-out (hostile goblins).

## Scope
- In: Hall arena, Fold scene, sleeper placements, tallies updating from facts, respawn rules content
- Out: Horn encounter (e13-horn-encounter)
- Out: Sleeper wake-up (e26-vesper-bell-finale)

## Notes
Chalk tallies read rescues.byHorn.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the player enters the Fold, when inside, then all seven sleepers are present on beds and fact fold.seen is set.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the player dies in the Knot with horn alive, when resolved, then they wake on a Fold moss bed and the tally shows one more mark.
- AC-3 [integration] Given horn.killed and goblins Hostile, when the player dies in the Knot, then they wake among the Forgotten in the Ossuary laying-out niche (edge).
- AC-4 [integration] Given the horn-key is pickpocketed while Horn rests, when used, then the Fold opens without combat.

items.title: Stage the Cradle arena for the abbot confrontation
items.description:
## Why
The heart of the Knot, where the dream leaks into the physical, is the final stage.

## What
As a player, I want a round chamber that bends toward its centre so that the finale feels dreamlike.
Place the four anchor lanterns (shootable, extinguishable), Hushling emergence points, Forgotten stirring positions, Tansy hostage position, Clatter's entrance, cover pillars, a balcony ring (archer), shadowed alcoves (thief), and the sorcerer's secret route arrival. Dream-leak zones (low gravity puddles / drifting objects) as world-property volumes.

## Scope
- In: Arena placement, anchor lanterns, spawn points, dream-leak volumes
- Out: Abbot encounter logic (e13-abbot-encounter)

## Notes
Dream-leak volumes use existing gravity/force properties only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the four anchor lanterns, when each is extinguished by any means, then the abbot's max health drops by 25%.
- AC-2 [integration] Given each class's Cradle replay, when run, then the encounter can be resolved by at least one path per class.
- AC-3 [integration] Given all lanterns destroyed before the abbot appears, when the encounter begins, then he relights one lantern (edge: encounter cannot be trivially skipped).
- AC-4 [perf] Given the Cradle fight with 4 Hushlings, 4 Forgotten and dream VFX, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent) and p95 <= 16.7 ms at 1080p on the Low preset on an Intel Iris Xe / base M1 8 GB class machine, with p99 <= 33.3 ms (30 fps floor) during worst-case combat.

items.title: Build the Sounding Shaft climb with defenders and chase variants
items.description:
## Why
With the tongue recovered, the bell must ring: a vertical ascent with the song rising behind.

## What
As a player, I want to climb from the Cradle to the belfry on ropes, counterweights and old bell-ropes so that the finale is a set piece.
Shaft interior: ledges, bell-rope climbs, counterweight lifts, a collapsing stair section. Variants by facts: Horn holds the foot (horn alive and healed/befriended); goblins or Clatter hold it; knight holds while restored Clatter climbs (sacrifice beat); nobody → chase with Hushlings climbing. Archer shortcut: rope line skips half the climb.

## Scope
- In: Shaft scene, climb routes, defender variants, chase spawner, archer shortcut
- Out: Ally behaviours (e14-horn-befriend-help)

## Notes
Falling during the chase drops the player to the last ledge checkpoint, not the bottom (anti-frustration).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given no defender facts, when the climb begins, then Hushlings spawn below and climb at 80% of player climb speed.
- AC-2 [integration] Given an archer fires a rope arrow into the marked beam, when climbed, then half the shaft is skipped.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player falls mid-climb, when they land, then they respawn on the last ledge checkpoint with the chase paused 3 s (edge).
- AC-4 [integration] Given the knight-hold variant, when chosen, then the player fights at the foot until the bell rings and Clatter completes the climb.

items.title: Ring the Vesper Bell: hang the tongue, mend it and wake the sleepers
items.description:
## Why
The solution is a lullaby. Ringing the cracked bell — wrong and beautiful — is the climax.

## What
As a player, I want to hang the bronze tongue and ring the bell so that the Nightjar sleeps and the missing wake.
Belfry finale: hang tongue (or Oswin's recast), optional mend first (Frostglass/Alteration-class property effect sets bell.mended for a truer note), ring. Song falters (song.intensity → 0), Hushlings dissolve, the Fold sleepers wake (sleepers.woken), Tansy asks who you are. Sets vespers.rung.

## Scope
- In: Tongue hang interaction, mend option, ring sequence, facts, dissolve/wake hooks
- Out: Endings text (e39-intro-endings-text)
- Out: Ending level states (e26-ending-states)

## Notes
Mend is systemic: any freeze or alteration effect applied to the crack entity counts.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the tongue hung, when the bell is rung, then vespers.rung is set, song.intensity becomes 0 and all Hushlings dissolve.
- AC-2 [integration] Given bell.mended before ringing, when rung, then the truer-note variant plays and fact bell.trueNote is set.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the tongue was destroyed and no recast exists, when the belfry is reached, then Oswin's recast path is signposted (edge: never unwinnable).

items.title: Wire dungeon shortcuts: crypt, cistern, cage lift and one-way doors
items.description:
## Why
Every loop is a shortcut the player can open; the dungeon should fold back on itself.

## What
As a player, I want to open doors from the far side and ride lifts back up so that returning to earlier areas is fast.
Shortcuts: crypt passage Knot ↔ priory (Horn opens, or pry from below), cistern ↔ priory (gate from the priory side), winch cage mine top ↔ bottom, supply-tunnel arrival ↔ goblin hall, Outer Ring ↔ Deepworks breach bypass. One-way doors with a visible "barred on this side" state.

## Scope
- In: Shortcut doors/lifts, facts, connectivity updates
- Out: Transition engine (e01-area-transitions)

## Notes
Each shortcut fact persists and shows on the world map notes.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a one-way door approached from the locked side, when interacted, then it shows the barred state and does not open.
- AC-2 [integration] Given each shortcut opened, when saved and reloaded, then it remains open.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the cage lift at the bottom and the player at the top, when the call lever is used, then the cage returns (edge: never stranded).

items.title: Author first-pass class routes through every dungeon area
items.description:
## Why
The knight forces, the thief infiltrates, the archer manipulates distant mechanisms, the sorcerer alters the dungeon.

## What
As a player of any class, I want each dungeon area to offer my class a route so that the Labyrinth plays differently for me.
Per area: knight (weak walls, heavy doors, holding chokepoints), archer (distant mechanisms, open-chamber dominance, rope anchors), sorcerer (freeze/levitate/blink/illusion affordances), thief (vents, crawlspaces, hidden passages, dark routes). Registry entries and replays.

## Scope
- In: Route affordances across mine/priory/Knot, registry entries, replays
- Out: Gap closing after audit (e16-gap-pass-dungeon)

## Notes
Every thief hidden passage should be discoverable by others too (with effort) — secrets are for everyone.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the registry, when validated, then every E26 mandatory obstacle has >= 3 class routes declared.
- AC-2 [integration] Given each declared route, when replayed, then the obstacle exit fact is set.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a thief hidden passage, when a non-thief searches the wall, then it can be found with a light or search action (edge).

items.title: Place dungeon secrets, notes, horn-coins and lore books
items.description:
## Why
Lore is offered, not lectured; the dungeon should reward every detour.

## What
As a curious player, I want hidden rooms, notes and relics so that I piece together the history myself.
Place 6–8 "friend below" notes, horn-coins (tiny ox asleep on the back), Hornfolk inscription fragments (sorcerer route), Mooring-era items, damaged spellbook pages, the Ox Beneath the Hill last page, 12–20 treasures per the e18 guide, and one book mimic trap per area.

## Scope
- In: Placements, discovery rules, facts
- Out: Text (e39-books-lore, e39-dialogue-abbot)

## Notes
Three sources that disagree for each big fact (bible §7.1).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the dungeon scenes, when audited, then every "friend below" note id from e39 is placed exactly once.
- AC-2 [content] Given the big facts (Long Vespers, the minotaur), when audited, then each has >= 3 placed sources (book, object, person).
- AC-3 [integration] Given a secret room opened, when saved and reloaded, then it stays open (edge).

items.title: Build the four endings' level states across town and dungeon
items.description:
## Why
Endings are assembled from world facts; the world itself should show the ending.

## What
As a player, I want the world to visibly change after my ending so that my choices feel real.
Fact-gated variants (e27-world-variants): Vespers Rung (bell rung each dusk by goblins/Hale/Tansy, bread at the mine gate, wolves howl again if breach sealed); The Last Warden (Horn's absence, goblin watch or Clatter humming, lantern and footprints at the gate); The Hireling's Silence (mine reopened, Vane prosperous, sleepwalker sitting up); The Long Vespers (sleeping valley, goblin with a stick in the Cradle).

## Scope
- In: Variant entity sets per ending in town, gate, Fold, Cradle; epilogue camera anchors
- Out: Ending logic and text (e39-main-quest-data, e39-intro-endings-text)

## Notes
Epilogue slides are text over these level states.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the facts for each ending, when the town and gate load, then the matching variant set is active and no other ending's variants are.
- AC-2 [integration] Given breach.sealed with Vespers Rung, when night falls in the Briarwood, then wolf howls resume.
- AC-3 [integration] Given contradictory facts (horn.killed and horn.befriended), when evaluated, then killed takes precedence and a content warning is logged (edge).

items.title: Art-dress the Deepworks and Bellwater Priory with final assets
items.description:
## Why
Timbered galleries and a roofless nave must read instantly as different places.

## What
As a player, I want the mine and the priory to look like the story bible so that each layer of the dungeon has its own identity.
Swap grey-box for mine kit (timber supports, rails, ore carts, goblin junk) and priory kit (Vesperine stone, singing statues, bell); keep gameplay ids and collision.

## Scope
- In: Art swap for Deepworks and priory scenes, LODs, decals
- Out: Asset creation (E37)

## Notes
Related: final assets come from E37/E38 per-asset prompt/generate/integrate beads created by the asset-prompt wave from plan/world-asset-needs.md; those integrate beads should block this item. Gameplay never waits on this item.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the dressed scenes, when all E26 route and puzzle replays in these areas run, then they pass unchanged.
- AC-2 [perf] Given the goblin hall and the nave, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).
- AC-3 [manual] Given the art review, when compared to the style bible, then silhouettes of interactables remain readable against dressing (edge).

items.title: Art-dress the Knot with Hornfolk stone, runes and dream visuals
items.description:
## Why
The Knot is a sentence carved as corridors; its art must make runes legible and the Cradle dreamlike.

## What
As a player, I want the labyrinth's walls to be written in Hornfolk runes and the Cradle to shimmer so that the place feels ancient and alive.
Hornfolk stone kit, rune band decals (readable, with landmark faces), bone niches, chapel acoustics visuals, Fold moss, Cradle dream-leak shaders.

## Scope
- In: Art swap for Knot scenes, rune decals, Cradle shaders
- Out: Asset creation (E37)

## Notes
Related: final assets come from E37/E38 per-asset prompt/generate/integrate beads created by the asset-prompt wave from plan/world-asset-needs.md; those integrate beads should block this item. Gameplay never waits on this item.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the dressed Knot, when rune-navigation tests and all Knot replays run, then they pass unchanged.
- AC-2 [perf] Given the Cradle fight with dream shaders, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).
- AC-3 [manual] Given 3 testers, when asked to follow runes, then >= 2 identify the rune to follow from art alone (edge: legibility).

items.title: Light and score the dungeon: mine, priory, Knot and the finale
items.description:
## Why
Darkness is a stealth system and a mood; the song must be heard growing.

## What
As a player, I want each dungeon layer to have its own light and sound so that descending feels like going deeper into a dream.
Lighting per area (lamps in the mine, moonlight in the priory, rune glow in the Knot), ambience beds (mine drips and creaks, priory wind, Knot hum, Chapel echoes), music cues per area plus the song layer driven by song.intensity, set-piece audio (sour bell, Horn's Hall, Cradle, climb, Vespers ring).

## Scope
- In: Lighting, ambience zones, reverb zones, music cue bindings, set-piece cue wiring
- Out: Audio assets (E38)

## Notes
Related: final assets come from E37/E38 per-asset prompt/generate/integrate beads created by the asset-prompt wave from plan/world-asset-needs.md; those integrate beads should block this item. Gameplay never waits on this item. Related: e28-ambience, e28-reverb-zones and e29-environment-fx are P2 in the combat plan; bind ambience beds, reverb zones and fog/firefly FX here when they land, otherwise ship lighting + music only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given song.intensity changes, when evaluated, then the song music layer gain follows within 2 s.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the Vespers ring, when triggered, then all other music ducks and the bell cue plays uninterrupted.
- AC-3 [integration] Given dungeon lighting, when sampled along each thief route, then at least 40% of each route has light <= 0.3 (edge: stealth remains viable).
- AC-4 [perf] Given the Chapel with 3 Hushlings and all area lights, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).

items.title: Perf-pass every dungeon area on both presets
items.description:
## Why
The dungeon hosts the heaviest fights and effects; it must hold budgets everywhere.

## What
Perf suite scenes for the goblin hall, scriptorium fire, Ossuary fight, Chapel, Horn's Hall, Cradle and the climb; captures on reference and low-tier machines; fixes within budget; area load times.

## Scope
- In: Perf scenes, captures, fixes, report
- Out: Engine-level perf (E32)

## Notes
Related: e32-reference-runbook, e32-memory-leak-test.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [perf] Given each listed dungeon perf scene, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).
- AC-2 [perf] Given the Cradle fight on Low, when measured, then p95 <= 16.7 ms at 1080p on the Low preset on an Intel Iris Xe / base M1 8 GB class machine, with p99 <= 33.3 ms (30 fps floor) during worst-case combat.
- AC-3 [perf] Given warm caches, when transitioning between any two adjacent dungeon areas, then load <= 3 s and heap <= 1.5 GB after 30 transitions (edge).

items.title: Playtest the full dungeon per class and replay each critical path
items.description:
## Why
The MVP's defining scenario must be completable and memorable for every class.

## What
Automated critical-path replays per class from the mine gate to "Vespers rung"; one internal playtest per class through the whole dungeon; findings to docs/playtests/dungeon.md with beads.

## Scope
- In: 4 critical-path replays, 4 playtests, findings
- Out: External playtests (e35-external-round-1)

## Notes
Replays must cover two different macro-routes per class across the four runs.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [e2e] Given a save at the mine gate, when each class's critical-path replay runs, then vespers.rung is set with zero console errors.
- AC-2 [manual] Given one tester per class, when finished, then each rates the dungeon >= 4/5 for "my class mattered".
- AC-3 [manual] Given testers who got stuck > 5 minutes, when observed, then each stuck point has a bead or accepted note (edge).

items.title: Block out Wendmouth harbour in grey-box with every named place
items.description:
## Why
Wendmouth is where shenanigans ensue; its layout decides every sightline, rooftop and heist route.

## What
As a player, I want a crooked, crowded harbour I can read in one visit so that I can plan mischief.
Grey-box (~200×160 m): Ore Wharf (barge berth, open Tidefair planking), Customs House, Bonded Warehouse, the fish market over the Undertow, the Tidemarket, net lofts, the breakwater with the Drowned Gull at its end, the pool with the Gilded Tern at anchor, towpath and barge arrival points. Warehouses on stilts with water beneath (standing-water volumes).

## Scope
- In: Harbour scene, building shells and entries, navmesh, water volumes, connectivity nodes, arrival spawns
- Out: Per-place content (other E40 items)
- Out: Art (e40-harbor-art-dress)

## Notes
Wendmouth is optional (bible §3.6): no main-quest edge may require it. The river does not flow in the sim; the harbour pool is standing water.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the scene, when validated, then every bible §3.6 place exists as a named node linked in connectivity.json.
- AC-2 [content] Given connectivity.json, when the main-quest critical path is computed, then no required edge passes through a Wendmouth node (edge: optional town).
- AC-3 [integration] Given the navmesh, when queried, then every building entry is reachable from both the barge berth and the towpath arrival.
- AC-4 [perf] Given the grey-box harbour from the Ore Wharf, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).

items.title: Build the Ore Wharf with working cranes, cargo nets and crate stacks
items.description:
## Why
The wharf is the harbour's toybox: swinging loads, cuttable nets and crate mazes for every class.

## What
As a player, I want cranes I can operate, nets I can cut and crates I can climb or hide behind so that the wharf invites hijinks.
Two cranes (operable winch + jib rotation, suspended loads on ropes), cargo nets (rope supports: cuttable, flammable, shootable), ore bins, stacked crates (climbable, hiding spots, pushable), the Lantern Court notice board, and the open planking marked for Tidefair events.

## Scope
- In: Crane mechanisms, net/rope entities, crate stacks with material presets, Tidefair space markers
- Out: Tidefair event logic (Tidefair items)
- Out: Heist hoist sequence (e40-crate-heist)

## Notes
Everything via properties: a net drops when its supporting rope is cut, burnt or shot — never scripted per weapon.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a loaded cargo net hanging from a crane, when its rope is severed by any means, then the load falls under physics and lands or splashes into the water volume below.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the crane jib rotated with a load swinging, when the load strikes a creature, then impulse damage applies via the damage model.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a crate stack pushed over, when it collapses onto the only walkway, then a climb or push route over the debris remains (edge: no softlock).

items.title: Build the Customs House, its strongroom and Cray's book confiscation
items.description:
## Why
Inspector Cray is the MVP's only on-screen Lantern Court official; confiscation turns carrying books into a story.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want a customs inspector who confiscates restricted books I carry openly so that smuggling them becomes my own heist.
Customs House: cargo scale, Cray's office (the well-read shelf, confiscated romances), the manifest copy of bay nine, the strongroom of confiscated goods (skylight/roof route, locked door). Inspection: at the barge berth and the customs gate, any book item with legality restricted and no writ in the player's visible inventory is moved to the strongroom as an owned-by-customs item (never forbidden-plot items). Recovery: buy back with a writ, steal back (a crime via e22-crime-bounty), or charm back (Contraband Pages).

## Scope
- In: Interior, strongroom container, inspection trigger + legality check, writ condition, confiscation facts
- Out: Contraband Pages quest graph (e39-side-quests-harbor)
- Out: Cray dialogue (e39-dialogue-harbor-trade)
- Out: Crime/bounty rules (e22-crime-bounty)

## Notes
Related: e21-stolen-forbidden-stock (P2) for reselling recovered restricted books. Stowaway arrivals (e25-barge-travel) and sneaking past the gate skip inspection.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the player carries a restricted book without a writ, when inspected, then the book moves to the strongroom container and fact customs.confiscated.<bookId> is set.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a book flagged as a plot item, when inspected, then it is never confiscated (edge).
- AC-3 [integration] Given a confiscated book stolen back from the strongroom while witnessed, when reported, then a Wendmouth crime is recorded via e22-crime-bounty.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the player holds a writ fact, when inspected, then nothing is confiscated and Cray's disposition is unchanged.

items.title: Build the Bonded Warehouse: bay nine, skylights, hoists and manifests
items.description:
## Why
The warehouse is the thief's showcase: a sealed bay, a watchman and a desk full of paper.

## What
As a thief, I want a warehouse with skylights, hoist beams and a manifest desk so that I can case it and choose my way in.
Sealed bays; bay nine (Vane Deepworks) with a customs-seal entity (intact / broken / re-sealed, stamp-verifiable); skylights (climb, rope-arrow anchor); hoist beams (traversable, can lower crates); the night watchman's patrol and lantern; the manifest desk (swap or forge the bay nine manifest); Jasper Quell's office (foundry invoice, honest manifest, Mr. S— letters).

## Scope
- In: Interior, seal state entity, skylight and beam routes, watchman patrol data, manifest desk and Quell's office items
- Out: Heist outcomes (e40-crate-heist)
- Out: Quell dialogue (e39-dialogue-harbor-trade)

## Notes
The seal records who stamped it; the dead clerk E. Ardley's stamp is evidence (bible canon).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the watchman's night patrol, when the stealth replay enters via a skylight, then bay nine can be reached with the watchman never exceeding Suspicious.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the bay nine seal broken, when re-sealed with the customs-seal stamp item, then the seal reads intact to inspection; without the stamp it reads broken.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the watchman finds a broken seal on his round, when perceived, then he raises the alarm and the harbour watch investigates (edge: failure creates pursuit, not reload).
- AC-4 [content] Given the obstacle registry, when validated, then bay nine declares >= 3 class routes.

items.title: Run data-defined contests with entry, scoring, cheating and bets
items.description:
## Why
The Tidefair and the Drowned Gull need contests; no other plan owns a contest runner, and bespoke scripting per event would not scale.

## What
A small data-driven contest runner in src/sim built on the condition/effect DSL and quest objective trackers: contest definitions {id, entry conditions, fee, participants, scoring from sim events, win/lose conditions, cheat rules (condition → detected-if-observed-by), betting book (odds, throw-the-match option), rewards/effects}. Emits contest.started/ended with placement.

## Scope
- In: Contest schema + validator, runner, cheat detection via perception of watchers, betting hook, outcome effects
- Out: Individual events (Tidefair items, e40-drowned-gull)
- Out: Quest graphs (e39-side-quests-harbor)

## Notes
Cheating is always possible and always has a consequence (bible §6.1 quest 7). Losing gracefully is a valid outcome with its own effect.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a contest with a scoring rule "hits on target tag gull", when 3 matching hit events occur, then the player score is 3 and ties break by earliest completion.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a cheat rule "magic used" and Cray perceiving the cast, when it occurs, then contest.cheatDetected fires and the disqualify effect applies; unobserved, no detection (edge).
- AC-3 [unit] Given the player accepts Nell's bet to throw the match, when they lose, then the payout effect applies; if they win, the betting-book grudge effect applies.
- AC-4 [content] Given contest data, when validated, then every contest has entry, win and lose conditions and references existing effects.

items.title: Build the Drowned Gull: arm-wrestling, dice, drinking and the trapdoor
items.description:
## Why
Nell's tavern is the harbour's social hub, the thief's drop point and a place where losing lands you somewhere new.

## What
As a player, I want a rowdy tavern where I can arm-wrestle Big Oona, drink, gamble, start or end a brawl and find the trapdoor to the Undertow so that Wendmouth's people become my allies or rivals.
Interior on the breakwater end: arm-wrestling table (contest), dice table, drinking contest (losing wakes you shanghaied in the Gilded Tern's hold via a wake-in-place rule), brawl trigger (non-lethal brawling), the thief commission drop with Nell (deliver the coin, keep it, or deliver a fake), and the trapdoor (found by search or granted by Nell's trust).

## Scope
- In: Interior, contest instances (arm-wrestling, dice, drinking), brawl trigger, drop interaction facts, trapdoor, wake rule
- Out: Nell and Oona dialogue (e39-dialogue-harbor-folk)
- Out: Tidefair brawl (e40-tidefair-strength)

## Notes
Brawls use non-lethal damage tags: knocked-out, never killed, for everyone involved.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the player loses the drinking contest, when it resolves, then they wake in the Tern's hold, fact tern.shanghaied is set and no reload occurs.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the thief delivers a fake horn-coin to Nell, when evaluated, then commission.fakeDelivered is set and the payout still occurs.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a brawl started in the tavern, when it ends, then no participant has died and the watch is not called (dockhands settle it).
- AC-4 [integration] Given the trapdoor is found without Nell's trust, when used, then the Undertow is reachable but Nell's disposition drops one band (edge).

items.title: Stage the Tidefair arm-wrestling bout and the Gull brawl
items.description:
## Why
Knights get hijinks too: beat Big Oona, then survive the free-for-all when someone loses badly.

## What
As a knight, I want to arm-wrestle and brawl at the Tidefair so that strength and timing win me coin and friends.
Arm-wrestling: a timed hold contest scored from stamina management and timed pushes (reuses e04 stamina). The Gull brawl: a non-lethal free-for-all on the wharf using melee and hit reactions with a knockout tag; environment pushes into the water are allowed. Both run on the contest framework with cheat rules (magic, dirty tricks) and a lose-gracefully branch (Oona buys you a drink).

## Scope
- In: Two contest definitions, arm-wrestle input/stamina binding, brawl non-lethal rules, participants
- Out: Combat systems (E04)
- Out: Quest rewards (e39-side-quests-harbor)

## Notes
Any class may enter; knights have the flavour advantage (poise, stamina).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the arm-wrestling contest, when the player outlasts Oona's stamina, then contest win fires and the Tidefair reputation fact increments.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the brawl, when any participant reaches 0 health, then they are knocked out (not killed) and leave the brawl.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player is shoved into the harbour during the brawl, when they surface, then they are out of the contest and may climb back via a ladder (edge).

items.title: Stage the Tidefair Gull Shoot and the Pocket Race
items.description:
## Why
Archers win shooting contests and thieves lift ribbons from five marks — one of them the Inspector.

## What
As an archer, I want to hit wooden gulls on a swinging boom and then the live gull that stole the ribbon; as a thief, I want to lift a ribbon from each of five marked contestants without being caught.
Gull Shoot: boom-mounted targets on a swinging rope (moving-target scoring), then a live harbour gull target that flees to the rooftops. Pocket Race: five marked NPCs wandering the wharf crowd (one is Cray), each carrying a ribbon; caught = out.

## Scope
- In: Two contest definitions, swinging boom prop, live-gull chase target, five marked contestants
- Out: Archery and pickpocket mechanics (E05/E10)

## Notes
Sabotage is possible: cut the boom rope, or plant a ribbon on a rival. Both have consequences via cheat rules.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the boom swinging, when an arrow hits a wooden gull, then the hit scores and the gull drops.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the Pocket Race, when the player lifts all five ribbons unseen, then they win; if Cray notices a lift, then she files a note (fact cray.noticedThief) but does not arrest.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the live gull flees to a rooftop, when the player follows, then its hoard location becomes reachable and the ribbon is retrievable (edge: prize never lost).

items.title: Stage the Tidefair Regatta rowing race on the harbour pool
items.description:
## Why
The sorcerer's hijinks: "no magic" is a rule nobody enforces until Cray walks by.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want to win a rowing race by gusting my sail or freezing a rival's oars so that magic creates comedy.
Boats are kinematic course-followers on the standing-water pool (no flow sim): speed from a rowing input rhythm, plus force stimuli on the sail (any impulse), minus frozen oars (frozen property halts a boat for 3 s). Cheat rule: magic observed by Cray disqualifies.

## Scope
- In: Boat kinematic course entity, rowing input, stimulus responses, contest definition
- Out: Boat physics or flowing water (not planned)

## Notes
True extra: cut first if schedule slips.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a force impulse applied to the player's sail, when evaluated, then boat speed rises by the impulse-derived boost for its duration.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a rival's oars frozen by any cold stimulus, when evaluated, then that boat halts for 3 s.
- AC-3 [integration] Given Cray perceives a cast during the race, when detected, then the player is disqualified and fact cray.regattaCheat is set (edge).

items.title: Author the Tidemarket: Tereza's arms stall and the foreign book cart
items.description:
## Why
Everyone can equip themselves better in Wendmouth than in Briar Glen; the Tidemarket is where.

## What
As a player of any class, I want an import market with foreign steel, light armour, exotic arrows and rare spellbooks so that the trip downriver upgrades my kit.
Merchant data on e20: Tereza Maelo's arms stall (curved Saltmarch sabres, harpoon-spears, lacquered round shields, sharkskin brigandine; an under-the-counter tier gated by duel/Tidefair facts); exotic arrows as foreign variants of MVP arrow types (whistling = noise, grapple = rope; data only); spice/silk/oddities stall. Foreign bookseller's cart authored on the e21 bookshop template (Storm, Illusion and Gravity texts; restricted ones subject to customs).

## Scope
- In: Covered market interior, three merchant files, one bookshop file, under-the-counter conditions
- Out: Arrow mechanics (E05)
- Out: Merchant dialogue (e39-dialogue-harbor-trade)
- Out: Tereza's duel (e40-tereza-duel)

## Notes
Related: e05-trick-arrows-extended (P3) — netting, tar and glass-headed arrows appear only if that lands. Mirela pays well for anything the cart won't sell (Related: e24-lamplit-stacks buyback).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the Tidemarket stock, when compared with all Briar Glen merchants, then every class has >= 2 purchasable items not sold in Briar Glen.
- AC-2 [content] Given the foreign book cart, when pnpm validate:bookshops runs, then it passes and no unique book is duplicated with the Lamplit Stacks.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the under-the-counter tier, when neither the duel nor a Tidefair win fact is set, then it is hidden (edge); with either, it appears.
- AC-4 [content] Given the arrow stock, when validated, then every arrow item references an existing e05 arrow type.

items.title: Stage Tereza Maelo's first-blood duel
items.description:
## Why
A retired duellist looking for a reason not to be: a knight's signature Wendmouth moment.

## What
As a knight, I want to accept Tereza's first-blood duel so that winning unlocks her under-the-counter stock and her respect.
Duel mode: non-lethal, first clean hit landed wins; Tereza uses a fast parry-heavy sabre move set (readability rules apply); dirty tricks count as a loss of honour (fact).

## Scope
- In: Duel encounter state, Tereza combat moves as creature data, outcome facts
- Out: Stall stock (e40-tidemarket)

## Notes
Any class may duel; knights receive the challenge unprompted.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given Tereza's move data, when validated, then every move passes the readability rule.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the player lands the first clean hit, when resolved, then tereza.duelWon is set and combat ends immediately with no further damage.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player uses a thrown distraction or poison during the duel, when detected, then tereza.dishonoured is set and the stock stays hidden (edge).

items.title: Build the Undertow black market and its smugglers' tunnels
items.description:
## Why
The Undertow sells what the Tidemarket can't — the thief's best tools — and links the harbour underground.

## What
As a thief, I want a black market in the smugglers' cellars with tunnels to the tavern and the harbour wall so that I can equip myself and move unseen.
Cellars beneath the fish market; tunnels to the Drowned Gull trapdoor and the breakwater sea-door; Nell Gannet's fence/merchant data: smuggler thief tools (tide-silk rope, glue-soled boots, smoke pearls, skeleton-key ring, customs-seal stamp), fenced goods, and the dockhand disguise kit item. Access: trust, the trapdoor, or the sea-door.

## Scope
- In: Cellar scene, tunnels, fence merchant data, thief tool item data (on e10 tool schema)
- Out: Tool mechanics (E10)
- Out: Disguise behaviour (e40-dockhand-disguises)

## Notes
Tool items reuse existing verbs: tide-silk rope → rope anchor, glue-soled boots → quieter footsteps on wet surfaces, smoke pearls → smoke escape, skeleton-key ring → lockpick bonus, customs-seal stamp → re-seal action.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given Nell's merchant file, when validated, then isFence is true and every tool references an existing capability or tool type.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the player enters by the sea-door, when first arriving, then the Undertow merchants are Wary rather than Hostile and trade is allowed after one exchange (edge).
- AC-3 [integration] Given the customs-seal stamp bought, when used on a broken seal, then the seal reads intact (ties to e40-bonded-warehouse).

items.title: Build a continuous rooftop and net-loft route across the waterfront
items.description:
## Why
Climbers should cross the whole harbour above the crowd — and archers need rigging-shot vantages.

## What
As a thief, I want a roof route from the Ore Wharf to the breakwater via net lofts so that I can reach skylights, the customs roof and the Tern's rigging line unseen.
Connected roofs and net lofts (hanging nets climbable and flammable), plank bridges, gull-hoard ledges, archer vantage points over the pool and the Tern's rigging.

## Scope
- In: Roof surfaces with acoustic tags, climbable nets, plank bridges, vantage points
- Out: Climbing mechanics (E10/E02)

## Notes
Tarred roofs are quiet; tin roofs are loud (acoustic tags).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the rooftop replay, when a thief crosses from the Ore Wharf to the breakwater, then they never touch street navmesh.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a climbable net ignited, when it burns, then the route segment closes and an alternative segment remains (edge).
- AC-3 [integration] Given an archer at a vantage point, when aiming at the Tern's hoist rope, then it is within effective bow range and unobstructed.

items.title: Build the Gilded Tern: rigging, hold, cabin, locked berth, departure
items.description:
## Why
The merchantman is the heist's destination, a shanghai wake point and a ship you can climb.

## What
As a player, I want to board the three-masted Tern by lighter, swim, rigging line, a frozen pool, Tereza's favour or signing on as crew so that the ship becomes a playground.
Ship at anchor in the pool: climbable rigging and yards, deck, hold (crates, shanghai wake spot), Captain Hesketh's cabin, the locked berth of Mr. S—'s agent (never opens in the MVP; interact hooks), crew patrols. World variant: when Act III begins the Tern is gone (fact tern.sailed) with or without Vane's crate.

## Scope
- In: Ship scene/area, rigging climb routes, hold and cabin, locked berth, boarding routes, sailed variant
- Out: Crew behaviour (e40-harbor-opposition)
- Out: Hesketh dialogue (e39-dialogue-harbor-trade)

## Notes
The pool is standing water: freezing it at night makes a walkable path to the hull (bible sorcerer route).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the pool frozen by any cold stimulus at night, when walked, then the Tern's hull ladder is reachable on foot.
- AC-2 [integration] Given fact act3.started, when the harbour loads, then the Tern is absent and tern.sailed is set; the crate outcome is recorded as shipped if not resolved.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player is on board when Act III starts, when the harbour next loads, then they are placed on the wharf, never stranded at sea (edge).
- AC-4 [content] Given the obstacle registry, when validated, then boarding the Tern declares >= 4 class routes.

items.title: Build the breakwater, sunken figurehead, sea-door and harbour tides
items.description:
## Why
Getting thrown off the pier should land you somewhere new: the figurehead and the smugglers' sea-door.

## What
As a player, I want being thrown off the pier to wash me up by a secret door so that failure in Wendmouth opens a route.
Stone breakwater, the sunken figurehead (debunks the sea-serpent rumour 18 by diving), the smugglers' sea-door into the Undertow tunnels. Harbour tide: two standing-water levels scheduled on the world clock (high/low); low tide exposes the sea-door and the crate-drop spot. Wake rule: "thrown off the pier" (subdued in Wendmouth) → surface at the breakwater.

## Scope
- In: Breakwater area, figurehead dive spot, sea-door, two-state tide schedule, wake rule content
- Out: Flowing water / waves (not planned)

## Notes
Tide is two scheduled water-level states, not simulation.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the player is subdued by dockhands or the watch in Wendmouth, when resolved, then they surface at the breakwater and harbor.thrownOffPier increments.
- AC-2 [integration] Given low tide on the clock schedule, when the harbour loads, then the sea-door is above water and enterable; at high tide it is reachable only by swimming (edge).
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player dives to the figurehead, when reached, then rumour 18 resolves as false.

items.title: Fill the harbour with pickpocketable crowds that give stealth cover
items.description:
## Why
Pickpocketable crowds make the thief's playground; market days should feel packed.

## What
As a thief, I want dense market-day crowds I can blend into and pick pockets from so that sneaking in plain sight is rewarded.
Crowd NPC sets on schedule windows (market days denser), each with a small pocket loot table; crowd volumes reduce the player's visibility score while moving at walk speed inside them; bumping a crowd NPC at run speed emits a noise/complaint.

## Scope
- In: Crowd schedule data, pocket loot tables, crowd-cover visibility modifier volumes, bump barks
- Out: Disguises (e40-dockhand-disguises)
- Out: Pickpocket mechanics (e10-pickpocketing)

## Notes
Crowd cover is a visibility modifier volume on e09-visibility-model inputs, not a new stealth system.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the player walking inside a crowd volume, when a watchman's visibility score is computed, then it is reduced by the configured crowd factor versus open ground.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a crowd NPC pickpocketed unseen, when checked, then an item from its pocket table is taken and no crime is recorded.
- AC-3 [perf] Given a market-day crowd of 40 agents on the Ore Wharf, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent) and p95 <= 16.7 ms at 1080p on the Low preset on an Intel Iris Xe / base M1 8 GB class machine, with p99 <= 33.3 ms (30 fps floor) during worst-case combat (edge: crowd LOD).

items.title: Let dockhand disguises fool the watch and warehouse crews
items.description:
## Why
A dockhand disguise from the Undertow is the classic heist entry.

## What
As a thief, I want a dockhand disguise that lets me walk into restricted wharf areas so that I can case the warehouse in daylight.
Disguise data for the dockhand faction look: accepted by harbour watch and warehouse crew until suspicious behaviour (running, climbing, entering bay nine, picking locks in view) exposes it.

## Scope
- In: Disguise definition, restricted-area rules, exposure behaviours for harbour factions
- Out: Disguise system (e10-disguises)

## Notes
Related: e40-crate-heist lists the disguise as one heist entry when this lands.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the disguise worn, when the player walks through the warehouse yard by day, then the watchman stays Unaware.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the disguised player climbs in view, when perceived, then the disguise is exposed and crime.disguise.exposed fires.
- AC-3 [integration] Given Nell's crew sees the disguise, when perceived, then they recognise it and do not report (edge: faction-specific).

items.title: Add the harbour watch, Low Tide Company and Tern crew as humans
items.description:
## Why
Wendmouth adds no creature types: its opposition is human and social — bribe, trick, drink with, out-brawl.

## What
As a player, I want harbour people who arrest, throw me off the pier or brawl instead of killing me so that getting caught in Wendmouth is a story.
Human creature data on e12: harbour watch (non-lethal by default; arrest via e22-crime-bounty or subdue → thrown off pier), Low Tide Company smugglers (clubs, knives, nets, whistles; alarms via whistles), Tern crew (deck patrols, belaying-pin clubs). Factions and relationships (Low Tide vs watch), bribe/drink affordances, retreat/surrender.

## Scope
- In: Three human archetypes as creature data, move sets, faction table entries, affordances, subdue outcomes
- Out: Crime/bounty (e22-crime-bounty)
- Out: Dialogue (e39-dialogue-harbor-folk, e39-dialogue-harbor-trade)

## Notes
Readability rules apply to human attacks too. Knives are lethal only if the player draws steel first (escalation fact).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the three human archetypes, when validated, then they pass CreatureDef and all moves pass readability.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the watch subdues the player without a bounty, when resolved, then the player is thrown off the pier (breakwater wake) rather than jailed.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a Low Tide smuggler blows a whistle, when heard by allies within range, then they converge on the whistle location.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the player bribes a watchman with enough coin, when accepted, then that watchman ignores trespass for 10 game minutes (edge: expires).

items.title: Add harbour gulls that steal shiny things and rats that give you away
items.description:
## Why
Ambient life with systemic hooks: gulls with criminal records and rats that squeal at the worst moment.

## What
As a player, I want gulls that snatch unattended shiny items and rats that scatter from light so that the harbour feels alive and mischievous.
Gulls: ambient agents that grab unattended items tagged shiny and fly to rooftop hoards (followable, lootable). Wharf rats: flee light, emit a startle noise event when a sneaking player passes within 1.5 m.

## Scope
- In: Two ambient agent definitions (not creature types), hoard containers, startle noise rule
- Out: Creature roster (stays at 10 types)

## Notes
Not counted as creature types (bible §8).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given an unattended shiny item on the wharf, when a gull reaches it, then it is carried to the nearest hoard container.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a sneaking player passes within 1.5 m of a rat, when evaluated, then a startle noise event is emitted that nearby watchers can hear.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a gull carrying a quest item, when it lands, then the item is placed in a reachable hoard (edge: quest items never lost).

items.title: Place The Crate for Mr. S— heist with all six solution routes
items.description:
## Why
The harbour's centrepiece: a stealth-first heist that every class can solve its own way.

## What
As a player of any class, I want to take Vane's relic crate by heist, paper, net, force, ice or leverage so that I win the name-stone and the manifest my way.
Wire the bible §6.1 quest 6 routes into the level: heist (case, roof/skylight entry, dodge the watchman, swap contents for ballast, re-seal with the stamp); paper (swap/forge the manifest so Cray seizes the crate legally, needing Quell's honest manifest or the dead clerk's seal); net (cut the net mid-hoist so the crate drops into the harbour, fish it out at low tide before the Low Tide Company); force (dockside brawl with Nell's crew and the watch; Cray arrives at the end); ice (freeze the pool at night and take it from the hold, or Gust the hoist so it lands on the wharf); leverage (confront Quell with the foundry invoice). Outcomes: name-stone, manifest, sealed letter facts.

## Scope
- In: Hoist sequence timing, crate entity with contents state, route wiring, outcome facts, low-tide retrieval spot
- Out: Quest graph (e39-harbor-heist-quest)
- Out: Disguise entry (Related: e40-dockhand-disguises, P2)

## Notes
Crate contents per canon: 40 horn-coins, 3 carved stones, 1 name-stone. The name-stone is a befriend-Horn trigger (Related: e14-horn-befriend-help).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given each of the six routes, when its replay runs, then the crate outcome fact is set to the route id and the name-stone is obtainable.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the perfect heist (contents swapped, seal re-stamped, no alert), when the Tern sails, then heist.perfect is set and no one in Wendmouth reacts.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the crate dropped into the harbour, when the Low Tide Company reaches it first at low tide, then the crate moves to the Undertow and remains obtainable there (edge: failure relocates).
- AC-4 [integration] Given Act III starts before any route resolves, when evaluated, then crate.shipped is set and the customs manifest copy still proves the shipments.

items.title: Declare Wendmouth obstacles and class routes in the registry
items.description:
## Why
Sneakiness is richly rewarded, but every class must get its hijinks; the audit has to see the harbour.

## What
As a player of any class, I want every harbour obstacle to offer my class a route so that Wendmouth plays to my fantasy.
Registry entries and replays for: customs strongroom, bay nine, boarding the Tern, the Undertow entry, the crate (six routes), and the Tidefair (one event per class flavour). Obstacles are marked mandatory within their quest (the town itself is optional).

## Scope
- In: Registry entries, route affordances added where missing, replays
- Out: Audit gate (e16-route-audit)

## Notes
Target 4 classes for bay nine and the Tern.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the registry, when validated, then every E40 quest-mandatory obstacle has >= 3 class routes and bay nine and the Tern have 4.
- AC-2 [integration] Given each declared route, when replayed, then the obstacle exit fact is set.
- AC-3 [integration] Given an obstacle whose only thief route needs the P2 disguise, when audited without it, then >= 3 other routes still pass (edge).

items.title: Place Wendmouth rumours, lore texts, secrets and treasure
items.description:
## Why
Rumours 13–18 must lead somewhere; every stilted warehouse should hide something.

## What
As a curious player, I want harbour gossip that points at real places so that talking in Wendmouth leads to mischief.
Bind rumours 13–18 to sources (Mags, Nell, Old Reed, Tidemarket gossip) with produced resolve facts; place the Lantern Court notice, the bay nine manifest copies, the foundry invoice, Mr. S—'s sealed letter; 10–14 treasures incl. smugglers' stashes and gull hoards.

## Scope
- In: Rumour source bindings, fact producers, lore/treasure placements
- Out: Texts (e39-harbor-rumors-texts)

## Notes
River rumour 16 resolves in e25-weeping-adit; 18 in e40-breakwater-sea-door.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given rumours 13–18, when validated, then each has >= 1 source and a resolvesWhen fact produced by placed content (no warnings).
- AC-2 [integration] Given rumour 15 heard, when the player enters the Undertow, then it resolves.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a stash looted, when saved and reloaded, then it stays empty (edge).

items.title: Art-dress Wendmouth with salt-bleached harbour assets and the Tern
items.description:
## Why
Tarred warehouses on stilts, net lofts and a three-master: Wendmouth must look loud and cheerful next to quiet Briar Glen.

## What
As a player, I want Wendmouth to look like a crooked, salt-bleached port so that arriving feels like a change of air.
Harbour kit, props, the Gilded Tern hero model, crowd variants, water surface materials; keep collision and gameplay ids intact.

## Scope
- In: Art swap for the harbour, the Tern, interiors, crowd visuals
- Out: Asset creation (E37)

## Notes
Related: final assets come from E37/E38 per-asset prompt/generate/integrate beads created by the asset-prompt wave from plan/world-asset-needs.md; those integrate beads should block this item. Gameplay never waits on this item.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the dressed harbour, when all E40 route and heist replays run, then they pass unchanged.
- AC-2 [perf] Given the Ore Wharf on market day with the Tern in view, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent) and draw calls <= 1500.
- AC-3 [manual] Given the art review, when compared to the style bible, then interactable affordances (climbable nets, cuttable ropes) remain legible against dressing (edge).

items.title: Light and score Wendmouth for market day, night and the tavern
items.description:
## Why
Loud and cheerful by day, lantern-lit and sneaky by night: the harbour's mood changes the play.

## What
As a player, I want Wendmouth to sound busy by day and to have dark pools of shadow at night so that both hijinks and heists feel right.
Lighting per phase (dock lanterns, ship lamps, lighthouse sweep on the breakwater), music cues (harbour day/night, Drowned Gull diegetic, Tidefair, heist tension), ambience bindings (gulls, rigging creak, surf), reverb zones for cellars.

## Scope
- In: Lighting, music bindings, ambience/reverb bindings
- Out: Audio assets (E38)

## Notes
Related: final assets come from E37/E38 per-asset prompt/generate/integrate beads created by the asset-prompt wave from plan/world-asset-needs.md; those integrate beads should block this item. Gameplay never waits on this item. Related: e28-ambience, e28-reverb-zones and e29-environment-fx are P2 in the combat plan; bind ambience beds, reverb zones and fog/firefly FX here when they land, otherwise ship lighting + music only.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the clock crosses dusk, when the phase event fires, then lighting blends to night within 5 s and music switches to the harbour night cue.
- AC-2 [integration] Given night lighting, when sampled along the warehouse heist routes, then >= 40% of each route has light <= 0.3 (edge: stealth viable).
- AC-3 [perf] Given night with all lanterns lit and the Tern's lamps, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).

items.title: Perf-pass and playtest Wendmouth on both presets
items.description:
## Why
Crowds, water, a ship and a brawl in one scene are a perf risk; hijinks must be discovered, not explained.

## What
Perf suite runs on market day, the Tidefair brawl and night heist scenes on reference and low-tier machines; a 5-tester playtest (one per class plus one free): do they find a hijink and a gear upgrade unprompted within 30 minutes? Findings in docs/playtests/wendmouth.md with beads.

## Scope
- In: Perf captures and fixes, playtest, findings
- Out: Global perf (E32)

## Notes
Related: e32-reference-runbook.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [perf] Given market day with 40 crowd agents on the Ore Wharf, when measured, then frame time p95 <= 16.7 ms (steady 60 fps) on the reference machine (MacBook Pro M1 Pro, Chrome, High preset, 1440p-equivalent).
- AC-2 [perf] Given the Tidefair brawl on Low, when measured, then p95 <= 16.7 ms at 1080p on the Low preset on an Intel Iris Xe / base M1 8 GB class machine, with p99 <= 33.3 ms (30 fps floor) during worst-case combat.
- AC-3 [perf] Given a warm cache, when arriving by barge, then the harbour is playable in <= 3 s and heap stays <= 1.5 GB.
- AC-4 [manual] Given 5 testers, when playing 30 minutes in Wendmouth, then >= 4 buy or earn a gear upgrade and >= 4 attempt a hijink or heist unprompted.
